plain_english: Now the path of space is also taught, through contraction and expansion, according to the method seen in the Shaiva scriptures.
sanskrit_cite: deśādhvano@pyatha samāsavikāsayogātsaṃgīyate vidhirayaṃ śivaśāstradṛṣṭaḥ

plain_english: The path of time, made of the Lord's power of action, has already been examined; now the path of space, connected with the variety of forms, is being defined.
sanskrit_cite: vicārito@yaṃ kālādhvā kriyāśaktimayaḥ prabhoḥ mūrtivaicitryajastajjo deśādhvātha nirūpyate

plain_english: This entire path is established in consciousness alone; whatever does not rest there is as unreal as a flower in the sky.
sanskrit_cite: adhvā samasta evāyaṃ cinmātre saṃpratiṣṭhitaḥ yattatra nahi viśrāntaṃ tannabhaḥkusumāyate

plain_english: Created through the door of consciousness, the path is situated in the void, in the intellect, in the vital airs, in the circles of channels, and also in the outer body.
sanskrit_cite: saṃviddvāreṇa tatsṛṣṭe śūnye dhiyi marutsu ca nāḍīcakrānucakreṣu barhirdehe@dhvasaṃsthitiḥ

plain_english: This path should be defined in this way, because by continually attending to its proper sequence the yogi can quickly attain the state of Bhairava.
sanskrit_cite: tatrādhvaivaṃ nirūpyo@yaṃ yatastatprakriyākramam anusaṃdadhadeva drāg yogī bhairavatāṃ vrajet

plain_english: When, by the mere desire to see, one abides pervading all things, what more needs to be said? So it is taught in the Spanda scripture.
sanskrit_cite: didṛkṣayaiva sarvārthān yadā vyāpyāvatiṣṭhate tadā kiṃ bahunoktena ityuktaṃ spandaśāsane

plain_english: Having known the entire path, one should dissolve it into its lords, and then, as before, melt them in sequence into the circle of body, breath, and mind.
sanskrit_cite: jñātvā samastamadhvānaṃ tadīśeṣu vilāpayet tān dehaprāṇadhīcakre pūrvavad gālayetkramāt

plain_english: All of that should be dissolved into one's own consciousness; when contemplated, that consciousness, full in its own nature, becomes the fire that dissolves the ocean of worldly existence.
sanskrit_cite: tatsamastaṃ svasaṃvittau sā saṃvidbharitātmikā upāsyamānā saṃsārasāgarapralayānalaḥ

plain_english: In the revered Mahikshottara, the teacher declared these lords of the path: Brahma rules from Ananta up to Pradhana, and Vishnu from Purusha up to Kala.
sanskrit_cite: śrīmahīkṣottare caitānadhveśān gururabravīt brahmānantātpradhānāntaṃ viṣṇuḥ puṃsaḥ kalāntagam

plain_english: Rudra rules in the knot, and Isha in Maya up to the range of Sadakhya; above them is the unsupported Shiva who pervades all that, and beyond him is the supreme who pervades even that.
sanskrit_cite: rudro granthau ca māyāyāmīśaḥ sādākhyagocare anāśritaḥ śivastasmādvyāptā tadvyāpakaḥ paraḥ

plain_english: Thus, understanding oneself as having attained Shiva-hood, it was defined in the Svacchanda teaching that this is not knowledge limited to mere procedure.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ śivatvamāpannamiti matvā nyarūpyata na prakriyāparaṃ jñānamiti svacchandaśāsane

plain_english: In the Trishiras teaching, awareness is conceived as root, middle, and tip, unfolding as the thirty-six principles, while memory is the construction of difference.
sanskrit_cite: triśiraḥśāsane bodho mūlamadhyāgrakalpitaḥ ṣaṭtriṃśattattvasaṃrambhaḥ smṛtirbhedavikalpanā

plain_english: The root of awareness is the 'I am' state with unobstructed distinction; it is the state of all principles, present in one's own self without division.
sanskrit_cite: avyāhatavibhāgo@smibhāvo mūlaṃ tu bodhagam samastatattvabhāvo@yaṃ svātmanyevāvibhāgakaḥ

plain_english: The middle of awareness is marked by a certain relation of support and supported, arising through the differentiation of the principles and the standing of each in its own nature.
sanskrit_cite: bodhamadhyaṃ bhavetkiṃcidādhārādheyalakṣaṇam tattvabhedavibhāgena svabhāvasthitilakṣaṇam

plain_english: The tip of awareness is clear, waveless, and full of vast bliss; it brings beings, states, bodies, and the rest into oneness with consciousness.
sanskrit_cite: bodhāgraṃ tattu vidbodhaṃ nistaraṅgaṃ bṛhatsukham saṃvidekātmatānītabhūtabhāvapurādikaḥ

plain_english: Unbroken consciousness is Bhairava, the supreme Lord; and in the revered Deviyayamala it is said that the path is beautiful with the thirty-six principles.
sanskrit_cite: avyavacchinnasaṃvittirbhairavaḥ parameśvaraḥ śrīdevyāyāmale coktaṃ ṣaṭtriṃśattattvasundaram

plain_english: By meditating on the sixfold path one can immediately become of the nature of Shiva, even though that Lord is not different from consciousness.
sanskrit_cite: adhvānaṃ ṣaḍvidhaṃ dhyāyansadyaḥ śivamayo bhavet yadyapyamuṣya nāthasya saṃvittyanatirekiṇaḥ

plain_english: For the full Lord there is no real arrangement of above, beginning, middle, or end; nevertheless, such distinctions are used for the sake of those who must understand and for the one who teaches.
sanskrit_cite: pūrṇasyordhvādimadhyāntavyavasthā nāsti vāstavī tathāpi pratipattṝṇāṃ pratipādayitustathā

plain_english: Conceptions such as middle and so forth arise according to one's own nature; therefore, by the limitation of the knower's conception, they regard the earthly principle as the lowest.
sanskrit_cite: svasvarūpānusāreṇa madhyāditvādikalpanāḥ tataḥ pramātṛsaṃkalpaniyamāt pārthivaṃ viduḥ

plain_english: That principle, standing in the innermost interval of all and covered by all the envelopes, is the earthly principle; here, within that earthly principle, the arrangement of worlds is described.
sanskrit_cite: tattvaṃ sarvāntarālasthaṃ yatsarvāvaraṇairvṛtam tadatra pārthive tattve kathyate bhuvanasthitiḥ

plain_english: The ruler of the Kataha Rudras, who are devoted to desire, is Ananta; he is mounted on a vessel within the waters, reeling from drinking liquor.
sanskrit_cite: netā kaṭāharudrāṇāmanantaḥ kāmasevinām potārūḍho jalasyāntarmadyapānavighūrṇitaḥ

plain_english: Meditating on the god Bhairava and surrounded by serpents, he is associated with the world of Kalagni above, which rises to a height of one crore yojanas.
sanskrit_cite: sa devaṃ bhairavaṃ dhyāyan nāgaiśca parivāritaḥ kālāgrerbhuvanaṃ cordhve koṭiyojanamucchritam

plain_english: For fear of reducing the worlds to ashes, he does not look upward; and although he pervades the universe, because he burns this earth he is understood in that lower position.
sanskrit_cite: lokānāṃ bhasmasādbhāvabhayānnordhva sa vīkṣate sa ca vyāptāpi viśvasya yasmātpluṣyannimāṃ bhuvam

plain_english: Because he was made clear earlier in relation to the hells, he is regarded as below them; the mighty one's flame extends ten crores, and above it there is an empty space of half that extent.
sanskrit_cite: narakebhyaḥ purā vyaktastenāsau tadadho mataḥ daśa koṭyo vibhorjvālā tadardha śūnyamūrdhvataḥ

plain_english: Above that level stand the lords of hell, feeling only pain in graded order, with some in the middle and others above, surrounded by intervals of difference.
sanskrit_cite: tadūrdhve narakādhīśāḥ kramādduḥkhaikavedanāḥ śdho madhye tadūrdhve ca sthitā bhedāntarairvṛtāḥ

plain_english: Among them, in order, are avici, kumbhipaka, and raurava, eleven and eleven and ten, ending at arrow-fire.
sanskrit_cite: avīcikumbhīpākākhyarauravāsteṣvanukramāt ekādaśaikādaśa ca daśetyantaḥ śarāgni tat

plain_english: For each of these there is a crore height interval, a lakh measure, and a duration between sky-void mouth counts.
sanskrit_cite: pratyekameṣāmekonā koṭirucchritirantaram lakṣamatra khavedāsyasaṃkhyānāmantarā sthitiḥ

plain_english: Above kushmanda, those who perform dark action contrary to scripture are placed in a lakh-less-crore station.
sanskrit_cite: kūṣmāṇḍa ūrdhve lakṣonakoṭisthānastadīśitā śāstraviruddhācaraṇāt kṛṣṇaṃ ye karma vidadhate

plain_english: There, terrible world-persons torment them until enjoyment ends, except those who once took refuge in supreme Shiva with one-pointed mind.
sanskrit_cite: tatra bhīmairlokapuruṣaiḥ pīḍyante bhogaparyantam ye sakṛdapi parameśaṃ śivamekāgreṇa cetasā śaraṇam

plain_english: They do not go hell-yoked; their dark result gives only small pleasure, with thousand-nine heights and one interval following in order.
sanskrit_cite: yānti na te narakayujaḥ kṛṣṇaṃ teṣāṃ sukhālpatādāyi sahasranavakotsedhamekāntaramatha kramāt

plain_english: In the eight patalas, one each, Hatuka is lord in the eighth; Shrikantha appoints selves per world and forces many.
sanskrit_cite: pātālāṣṭakamekaikamaṣṭame hāṭakaḥ prabhuḥ pratilokaṃ niyuktātmā śrīkaṇṭho haṭhato bahūḥ

plain_english: Thus that one gives powers in the raurava rule to vow-keepers and those who perform forbidden conduct.
sanskrit_cite: siddhīrdadātyasāvevaṃ śrīmadrauravaśāsane vratino ye cikarmasthā niṣiddhācārakāriṇaḥ

plain_english: Even initiated persons who lose their vow and do not perform penances become corrupters of left conduct in that place.
sanskrit_cite: dīkṣitā api ye luptasamayā naca kurvate prāyaścittāṃstathā tatsthā vāmācārasya dūṣakāḥ

plain_english: Those living by shares of god, fire, and substance stand highest; others below are devoted to garuda and other mantras.
sanskrit_cite: devāgnidravyavṛttyaṃśajīvinaścottamasthitāḥ adhaḥsthagāruḍādyanyamantrasevāparāyaṇāḥ

plain_english: They are various servants before Hatuka; but if there they worship the god-lord with devotion, they are transformed.
sanskrit_cite: te hāṭakavibhoragre kiṅkarā vividhātmakāḥ te tu tatrāpi deveśaṃ bhaktyā cetparyupāsate

plain_english: They dissolve in that lord-principle and gradually reach supreme Shiva; otherwise they remain engaged in that enjoyment.
sanskrit_cite: tadīśatattve līyante kramācca parame śive anyathā ye tu vartante tadbhoganiratātmakāḥ

plain_english: They, devoted to crying under time-fire torment, dissolve in the quality-principle and then return again at creation's mouth.
sanskrit_cite: te kālavahnisaṃtāpadīnākrandaparāyaṇāḥ guṇatattve nilīyante tataḥ sṛṣṭimukhe punaḥ

plain_english: They are cast by mothers with terrible torment into lowest-low bodies, according to their own action.
sanskrit_cite: pātyante mātṛbhirghorayātanaughapurassaram adhamādhamadeheṣu nijakarmānurūpataḥ

plain_english: Among humans there, some mantra-knowers are freed in order, but others are bound according to prior deed.
sanskrit_cite: mānuṣānteṣu tatrāpi kecinmantravidaḥ kramāt mucyante@nye tu badhyante pūrvakṛtyānusārataḥ

plain_english: Thus this group account, named hulahula and so on, is spoken by the blessed one in the shrimad ananda-adhika rule.
sanskrit_cite: ityeṣa gaṇavṛttānto nāmnā hulahulādinā proktaṃ bhagavatā śrīmadānandādhikaśāsane

plain_english: Above patala are thousands and twenty earth-bowl; in siddha tantra, on patala's back, it is surrounded by yakshi.
sanskrit_cite: pātālordhve sahasrāṇi viṃśatirbhūkaṭāhakaḥ siddhātantre tu pātālapṛṣṭhe yakṣīsamāvṛtam

plain_english: Adepts play with them at Bhadrakali's city; then dark hot earth, then void, then horse.
sanskrit_cite: bhadrakālyāḥ puraṃ yatra tābhiḥ krīḍanti sādhakāḥ tatastamastaptabhūmistataḥśūnyaṃ tato@hayaḥ

plain_english: These are torment places for corrupters of guru-mantra and the like; then above earth and middle to Meru, thousands and sixteen.
sanskrit_cite: etāni yātanāsthānaṃ gurumantrādidūṣiṇām tato bhūmyūrdhva [madhya] to meruḥ sahasrāṇi sa ṣoḍaśa

plain_english: Its root is submerged and spread, its height is thousand-ocean-vasu, and it is the golden abode of all gods.
sanskrit_cite: magnastanmūlavistārastaddvayenordhvavistṛtiḥ sahasrābdhivasūcchrāyo haimaḥ sarvāmarālayaḥ

plain_english: Middle-above-below is a risen arrow-bowl square; Bhairavi and that linga are named, and earth is its pedestal.
sanskrit_cite: madhyordhvādhaḥ samudvṛttaśarāvacaturaśrakaḥ bhairavīyaṃ ca talliṅgaṃ dharaṇī cāsya pīṭhikā

plain_english: All gods are indeed dissolved there; that is always worshipped in the middle, in the Meru assembly, with element and lord-direction banner.
sanskrit_cite: sarve devā nilīnā hi tatra tatpūjitaṃ sadā madhye merusabhā dhātustadīśadiśi ketanam

plain_english: Shambhu's light-peak and Shrikantha's part are that lord; descending, thousands and fourteen of Manovati.
sanskrit_cite: jyotiṣkaśikharaṃ śaṃbhoḥ śrīkaṇṭhāṃśaśca sa prabhuḥ avaruhya sahasrāṇi manovatyāścaturdaśa

plain_english: Here at Meru is a four-direction circle-wall; world-guardians are placed east and south of Amaravati's center.

plain_english: The verse names a world, its inhabitants, and a direction around Meru.

plain_english: The verse names a world, its inhabitants, and a direction around Meru.

plain_english: The verse names a world, its inhabitants, and a direction around Meru.

plain_english: The verse names a world, its inhabitants, and a direction around Meru.

sanskrit_cite: etairbhuvamavaṣṭabhya merustiṣṭhati niścalaḥ caitrarathanandanākhye vaiśrājaṃ pitṛvanaṃ vanānyāhuḥ

plain_english: The verse names a world, its inhabitants, and a direction around Meru.
sanskrit_cite: raktodamānasasitaṃ bhadraṃ caitaccatuṣṭayaṃ sarasām vṛkṣāḥ kadambajambvaśvatthanyagrodhakāḥ kramaśaḥ

plain_english: The verse names a world, its inhabitants, and a direction around Meru.
sanskrit_cite: eṣu ca caturṣvacaleṣu trayaṃ trayaṃ kramaśa etadāmnātam mervadho lavaṇābdhyantaṃ jambudvīpaḥ samantataḥ

plain_english: The verse names a world, its inhabitants, and a direction around Meru.
sanskrit_cite: lakṣamātraḥ sa navadhā jāto maryādaparvataiḥ niṣadho hemakūṭaśca himavāndakṣiṇe trayaḥ

plain_english: The verse names a world, its inhabitants, and a direction around Meru.

sanskrit_cite: jāṭharaḥ kūṭahimavadyātrajārudhiśṛṅgiṇaḥ evaṃ sthito vibhāgo@tra varṣasiddhyai nirūpyate

plain_english: The verse names a world, its inhabitants, and a direction around Meru.
sanskrit_cite: samantāccakravāṭādho@narkendu caturaśrakam sahasranavavistīrṇamilākhyaṃ trimukhāyuṣam

plain_english: The verse names a world, its inhabitants, and a direction around Meru.
sanskrit_cite: meroḥ paścimato gandhamādo yastasya paścime ketumālaṃ kulādrīṇāṃ saptakena vibhūṣitam

plain_english: The verse names a world, its inhabitants, and a direction around Meru.
sanskrit_cite: meroḥ pūrva mālyavānyo bhadrāśvastasya pūrvataḥ sahasradaśakāyustatsapañcakulaparvatam

plain_english: The verse names a world, its inhabitants, and a direction around Meru.
sanskrit_cite: pūrvapaścimataḥ savyottarataśca kramādime dvātriṃśacca catustriṃśatsahasrāṇi nirūpite

plain_english: The verse names a world, its inhabitants, and a direction around Meru.
sanskrit_cite: merorudak śṛṅgavānyastadbahiḥ kuruvarṣakam cāpavannavasāhasramāyustatra trayodaśa

plain_english: North of Kuruvarsha, in the northwest ocean, there are ten lakes in order, extending for thousands, and there are two islands, Chandra and Bhadraka.
sanskrit_cite: kuruvarṣasyottare@tha vāyavye@bdhau kramāccharāḥ daśa ceti sahasrāṇi dvīpau candro@tha bhadrakaḥ

plain_english: On the left side of Meru stand two white-peaked mountains, and between them lies Hiranmaya, nine thousand in extent, where the lifespan is twelve and a half.
sanskrit_cite: yau śvetaśṛṅgiṇau merorvāme madhye hiraṇmayam tayornavakavistīrṇamāyuścārdhatrayodaśa

plain_english: There, to the left, between the Shveta and Nila mountains, lies Ramyaka, nine thousand in extent, where the lifespan is twelve.
sanskrit_cite: tatra vai vāmataḥ śvetanīlayo ramyako@ntare sahasranavavistīrṇamāyurdvādaśa tāni ca

plain_english: South of Meru are the mountains Hema and Nishadha, and between them lies Harivarsha, nine thousand in extent, where the lifespan is a thousand more.
sanskrit_cite: merordakṣiṇato hemaniṣadhau yau tadantare haryākhyaṃ navasāhasraṃ tatsahasrādhikāyuṣam

plain_english: Farther south, between Hema and Himavat, lies Kimpurusha, nine thousand in extent, where the lifespan is a thousand more.
sanskrit_cite: tatraiva dakṣiṇe hemahimavaddvitayāntare kainnaraṃ navasāhasraṃ tatsahasrādhikāyuṣam

plain_english: South of Himavat lies Bharata, nine thousand in extent, the lowest land where beings both perform action and experience its fruits.
sanskrit_cite: tatraiva dakṣiṇe merorhimavānyasya dakṣiṇe bhārataṃ navasāhasraṃ cāpavatkarmabhogabhūḥ

plain_english: Ilavrita, Ketubhadra, Kuru, Hairanya, Ramyaka, and the regions of Hari and Kimpurusha are lands of enjoyment, but not lands of action.
sanskrit_cite: ilāvṛtaṃ ketubhadraṃ kuruhairaṇyaramyakam harikinnaravarṣe ca bhogabhūrna tu karmabhūḥ

plain_english: In those regions, although they are mainly not lands of action, even animals may acquire karmic impressions because of firmly established prior conditioning.
sanskrit_cite: atra bāhulyataḥ karmabhūbhāvo@trāpyakarmaṇām paśūnāṃ karmasaṃskāraḥ syāttādṛgdṛḍhasaṃskṛteḥ

plain_english: Even beings without present impressions may appear in Bharata or elsewhere, and through firm prior impressions or by the Lord's will they may still experience good and bad results.
sanskrit_cite: saṃbhavantyapyasaṃskārā bhārate@nyatra cāpi hi dṛḍhaprāktanasaṃskārādīśecchātaḥ śubhāśubham

plain_english: Action is also found in other places, as the ancient tradition says; there the time is always Treta, but in Bharata the full cycle of four ages prevails.
sanskrit_cite: sthānāntare@pi karmāsti dṛṣṭaṃ tacca purātane tatra tretā sadā kālo bhārate tu caturyugam

plain_english: In Bharata there are nine divisions separated by ocean water; the land measures five hundred and the water measures five hundred as well.
sanskrit_cite: bhārate navakhaṇḍaṃ ca sāmudreṇāmbhasātra ca sthalaṃ pañcaśatī tadvajjalaṃ ceti vibhajyate

plain_english: The divisions are Indra, Kasheru, Tamrabha, Naga, eastern Gabhastimat, Saumya, Gandharva, Varaha, and the one called Kanya, extending up to the ocean.
sanskrit_cite: indraḥ kaśerustāmrābho nāgīyaḥ prāggabhastimān saumyagāndharvavārāhāḥ kanyākhyaṃ cāsamudrataḥ

plain_english: In the ninth division, Kanya island, there are six sub-islands situated to the south in the middle of the ocean, and the island is adorned by seven chief mountains.
sanskrit_cite: kanyādvīpe ca navame dakṣiṇenābdhimadhyagāḥ upadvīpāḥ ṣaṭ kulādrisaptakena vibhūṣite

plain_english: The mountains are Anga, Yava, Malaya, Shanku, Kumuda, and Varaha; Agastya dwells on Malaya, and Lanka stands on Trikuta—these are the six sub-islands.
sanskrit_cite: aṅgayavamalayaśaṅkuḥ kumudavarāhau ca malayago@gastya tatraiva ca trikūṭe laṅkā ṣaḍamī hyupadvīpāḥ

plain_english: The islands and sub-islands are inhabited mostly by various foreign peoples and are rich in pearls, gold, and gems, as stated in the teaching of Shri Ruru.
sanskrit_cite: dvīpopadvīpagāḥ prāyo mlecchā nānāvidhā janāḥ muktākāñcanaratnāḍhyā iti śrīruruśāsane

plain_english: Whatever action is done in Bharata can be exhausted there, and by it one may reach from the lowest hell up to Shiva, or even attain liberation—especially in the region called Kanya.
sanskrit_cite: bhārate yatkṛtaṃ karma kṣapitaṃ vāpyavīcitaḥ śivāntaṃ tena muktirvā kanyākhye tu viśeṣataḥ

plain_english: In Bharata dwell Mahakala and a crore of Rudras, and there flow the Ganga and five hundred other sacred streams; therefore birth here is extremely hard to obtain.
sanskrit_cite: mahākālādikā rudrakoṭiratraiva bhārate gaṅgādipañcaśatikā janma tenātra durlabham

plain_english: In other regions beings pass through their karma by mere enjoyment, like animals, but for those born in Bharata even attainments beyond desire are possible.
sanskrit_cite: anyavarṣeṣu paśuvad bhogātkarmātivāhanam prāpyaṃ manorathātītamapi bhāratajanmanām

plain_english: Because Kanya island has the full variety of classes, stages of life, conduct, pleasures, and pains, it is a land of action and the supreme one.
sanskrit_cite: nānāvarṇāśramācārasukhaduḥkhavicitratā kanyādvīpe yatastena karmabhūḥ seyamuttamā

plain_english: Here, those who perform good and bad deeds attain the higher and lower results of heaven and hell, as stated in the Raurava-varttika.
sanskrit_cite: puṃsā sitāsitānyatra kurvatāṃ kila siddhyataḥ parāparau svarnirayāviti rauravavārtike

plain_english: Thus the region below Meru around Jambu, when described in detail, is divided into seventeen parts, but in summary into nine.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ meroradho jambūrabhito yaḥ sa vistarāt syāt saptadaśadhā khaṇḍairnavabhistu samāsataḥ

plain_english: Svayambhuva Manu had ten sons; later three departed, and in the land called Jambu the king was Agnidhra.
sanskrit_cite: manoḥ svāyaṃbhuvasyāsan sutā daśa tatastrayaḥ prāvrajannatha jambvākhye rājā yo@gnīdhranāmakaḥ

plain_english: Agnidhra had nine sons, and from them came the ninefold division; Nabhi was the ninth, and his grandson was Bharata, the son of Rishabha.
sanskrit_cite: tasyābhavannava sutāstato@yaṃ navakhaṇḍakaḥ nābhiryo navamastasya naptā bharata ārṣabhiḥ

plain_english: Bharata had eight sons and one daughter, making a ninth share; they divided and enjoyed that territory of one lakh yojanas in nine parts.
sanskrit_cite: tasyāṣṭau tanayāḥ sākaṃ kanyayā navamoṃ@śakaḥ bhuktaistairnavadhā tasmāllakṣayojanamātrakāt

plain_english: The salt ocean measures one hundred thousand yojanas. Outside it stand mountains, and to the north are Rishabha, Dundubhi, Dhumra, Kanka, Drona, and Indu.
sanskrit_cite: lakṣaikamātro lavaṇastadbāhye@sya puro@drayaḥ ṛṣabho dundubhirdhūmraḥ kaṅkadroṇendavo hyudak

plain_english: To the west stand Varaha, Nandana, Ashoka, and Balahaka. To the south stand Chakra and Mainaka, and between those two is the submarine fire.
sanskrit_cite: varāhanandanāśokāḥ paścāt sahabalāhakau dakṣiṇa cakramainākau vāḍavo@ntastayoḥ sthitaḥ

plain_english: South of the ocean, two thousand yojanas away, stands the mountain Vidyutvan, three thousand yojanas high and wide. There live people who eat fruit.
sanskrit_cite: abdherdakṣiṇataḥ khākṣisahasrātikramād giriḥ vidyutvāṃstrisahasrocchridāyāmo@tra phalāśinaḥ

plain_english: They are smeared with dirt, have long hair and beards, go naked, and behave like cows. They live for eighty years and eat grass.
sanskrit_cite: maladigdhā dīrghakeśaśmaśravo gosadharmakāḥ nagnāḥ saṃvatsarāśītijīvinastṛṇabhojinaḥ

plain_english: There are always unbarred doors there for entering the netherworld. This is taught by the teachers in the revered Raurava scripture.
sanskrit_cite: niryantrāṇi sadā tatra dvārāṇi bilasiddhaye ityetad gurubhirgītaṃ śrīmadrauravaśāsane

plain_english: Thus the salt ocean has been described. Beyond it lie six continents, and each one is surrounded by its own ocean.
sanskrit_cite: itthaṃ ya eṣa lavaṇasamudraḥ pratipāditaḥ tadbahiḥ ṣaḍamī dvīpāḥ pratyekaṃ svārṇavairvṛtāḥ

plain_english: The six continents, each successively doubled in size and ruled by six sons of Manu, are Shaka, Kusha, Krauncha, Shalmali, Gomeda, and Pushkara. Their six oceans are of milk, curd, ghee, sugarcane juice, liquor, and sweet water.
sanskrit_cite: kramadviguṇitāḥ ṣaḍbhirmanuputrairadhiṣṭhitāḥ śākakuśakrauñcāḥ śalmaligomedhābjamiti ṣaḍdvīpāḥ kṣīradadhisarpiraikṣavamadirāmadhurāmbukāḥ ṣaḍambudhayaḥ

plain_english: Medhatithi, Vapushmat, Jyotishmat, Dyutimat, King Havi, and Samvara rule Shaka and the other continents, and Agnidhra was appointed over Jambu continent.
sanskrit_cite: medhātithirvapuṣmāñjyotiṣmāndyutimatā havī rājā saṃvara iti śākādiṣu jambudvīpe nyarūpi cāgnīdhraḥ

plain_english: The five continents beginning with Shaka are each divided into regions by seven mountains. Pushkara is divided into two parts, and there Hari, Yama, Varuna, and Indra rule in the east and the other directions.
sanskrit_cite: girisaptakaparikalpitatāvatkhaṇḍāstu pañca śākādyāḥ puṣkarasaṃjño dvidalo hariyamavaruṇendavo@tra pūrvādau

plain_english: From half of Meru up to the end of the sweet-water ocean, the total measure is two crores, fifty-three lakhs, and fifty thousand yojanas.
sanskrit_cite: tripañcāśacca lakṣāṇi dvikoṭyayutapañcakam svādvarṇavāntaṃ mervardhādyojananāmiyaṃ pramā

plain_english: Beyond the seventh ocean lies a golden land extending ten crores of yojanas. After that is the Lokāloka mountain, one hundred thousand yojanas high and ten thousand yojanas broad.
sanskrit_cite: saptamajaladherbāhye haimī bhūḥ koṭidaśakamatha lakṣam ucchrityā vistārādayutaṃ loketarācalaḥ kathitaḥ

plain_english: Eight Rudras with the world-lords are stationed in the eight directions of Lokāloka. Some say the sun moves only within Lokāloka and never goes beyond it.
sanskrit_cite: lokālokadigaṣṭaka saṃsthaṃ rudrāṣṭakaṃ salokeśam kevalamityapi kecillokālokāntare ravirna bahiḥ

plain_english: The paths of the ancestors and the gods, going south and north, are the sun's two tracks. Teachers say these are the sun's southern and northern courses.
sanskrit_cite: pitṛdevapathāvasyodagdakṣiṇagau svajātpare vīthyau bhānoruttaradakṣiṇamayanadvayametadeva kathayanti

plain_english: Meru is north of all and Lokāloka is south. In this way one should understand the sun's rising and setting.
sanskrit_cite: 'sarveṣāmuttaro merurlokālokaśca dakṣiṇaḥ.' udayāstamayāvitthaṃ sūryasya paribhāvayet

plain_english: When it is midnight in Amaravati, it is sunset in Yama's city, midday in Varuna's city, and sunrise in Soma's city.
sanskrit_cite: ardharātro@marāvatyāṃ yāmyāyāmastameva ca madhyandinaṃ tadvāruṇyāṃ saumye sūryodayaḥ smṛtaḥ

plain_english: When it is sunrise in Amaravati, it is midnight in Yama's abode, sunset in Soma's city, and midday in Varuna's city. Thus the times change with the sun's movement.
sanskrit_cite: udayo yo@marāvatyāṃ so@rdharātro yamālaye ke@staṃ saumye ca madhyāhna itthaṃ sūryagatāgate

plain_english: Beyond the Lokāloka mountain lies darkness extending thirty-five hundred crores, nineteen lakhs, and forty thousand yojanas.
sanskrit_cite: pañcatriṃ śatkoṭisaṃkhyā lakṣāṇyekonaviṃśatiḥ catvāriṃśatsahasrāṇi dhvāntaṃ lokācalādbahiḥ

plain_english: Beyond Lokāloka lies the Garbhoda ocean, the king of oceans, equal in measure to the seven oceans. In its womb rests the entire earth.
sanskrit_cite: saptasāgaramānastu garbhodākhyaḥ samudrarāṭ lokālokasya parato yadgarbhe nikhilaiva bhūḥ

plain_english: According to the Siddhanta scripture, on the shore of the Garbhoda ocean is a region called Kausheya. There Garuda lives surrounded by accomplished birds.
sanskrit_cite: siddhātantre@tra garbhābdhestīre kauśeyasaṃjñitam maṇḍalaṃ garuḍastatra siddhapakṣasamāvṛtaḥ

plain_english: There they sport on mountain tops, and there are nine principal mountains. Beyond them are thirty hot-water rivers that flow down to the netherworld.
sanskrit_cite: krīḍantiṃ parvatāgre te nava cātra kulādrayaḥ tata uṣṇodakāstriṃśannadyaḥpātālagāstataḥ

plain_english: Then comes the Naimi garden in the four directions, always attended by yoginis. After that are Meru, the serpents, the clouds, and then the golden egg.
sanskrit_cite: caturdiṅnaimirodyānaṃ yoginīsevitaṃ sadā tato merustato nāgā meghā hemāṇḍakaṃ tataḥ

plain_english: Enclosed by the shell of Brahma's egg, the world called Bhurloka extends fifty crores of yojanas in the ten directions.
sanskrit_cite: brahmaṇo@ṇḍakaṭāhena merorardhena koṭayaḥ pañcāśadevaṃ daśasu dicu bhūrlokasaṃjñitam

plain_english: This earth-world is filled with six kinds of beings: beasts, birds, deer, trees, humans, and reptiles. It is also inhabited by pishachas, rakshasas, gandharvas, and yakshas.
sanskrit_cite: paśukhagamṛgatarumānuṣasarīsṛpaiḥ ṣaḍbhireṣa bhūrlokaḥ vyāptaḥ piśācarakṣogandharvāṇāṃ sayakṣāṇām

plain_english: It is also the abode of vidyadharas, and in short, for the whole creation of beings it serves as a place of enjoyment and residence according to their desire.
sanskrit_cite: vidyābhṛtāṃ ca kiṃ vā bahunā sarvasya bhūtasargasya abhimānato yatheṣṭaṃ bhogasthānaṃ nivāsaśca

plain_english: Between bhuvarloka and the sun there are ten wind paths, each separated by ten thousand units.
sanskrit_cite: bhuvarlokastathā tvārkāllakṣamekaṃ tadantare daśa vāyupathāste ca pratyekamayutāntarāḥ

plain_english: The first wind path above is ritarddhi, fifty yojanas above.
sanskrit_cite: ādyo vāyupathastatra vitataḥ paricarcyate pañcāśadyojanordhve syādṛtarddhirnāma mārutaḥ

plain_english: The nourishing wind is followed by pracetas, higher by a hundred.
sanskrit_cite: āpyāyakaḥ sa jantūnāṃ tataḥ prācetaso bhavet pañcāśadyojanādūrdhva tasmādūrdhva śatena tu

plain_english: Mute lightning clouds stand a krosa from earth and shower rain.
sanskrit_cite: senānīvāyuratraite mūkameghāstaḍinmucaḥ ye mahyāḥ krośamātreṇa tiṣṭhanti jalavarṣiṇaḥ

plain_english: Above them are clouds showering frogs and beings, and higher poison-water clouds.
sanskrit_cite: tebhya ūrdhva śatānmeghā bhekādiprāṇivarṣiṇaḥ pañcāśadūrdhvamogho@tra viṣavāripravarṣiṇaḥ

plain_english: Skanda-born clouds and pisacas occur in the flood wind; fifty above are maraka clouds.
sanskrit_cite: meghāḥ skandodbhavāścānye piśācā oghamārute tataḥ pañcāśadūrdhvaṃ syurmeghā mārakasaṃjñakāḥ

plain_english: Mahadeva-born vinayakas there take away the actions of unperfected men.
sanskrit_cite: tatra sthāne mahādevajanmānaste vināyakāḥ ye haranti kṛtaṃ karma narāṇāmakṛtātmanām

plain_english: Fifty above is vajranka wind, with stone clouds and lowest vidyadharas.
sanskrit_cite: pañcāśadūrdhvaṃ vajrāṅko vāyuratropalāmbudāḥ vidyādharādhamāścātra vajrāṅke saṃpratiṣṭhitāḥ

plain_english: Those who died with siddhi are situated in vajranka wind.
sanskrit_cite: ye vidyāpauruṣe ye ca śmaśānādiprasādhane mṛtāstatsiddhisiddhāste vajrāṃke maruti sthitāḥ

plain_english: Fifty above vajranka are electric rain clouds, apsarasas, and merit-doing men.
sanskrit_cite: pañcāśadūrdhvaṃ vajrāṃkādvaidyuto@śanivarṣiṇaḥ abdā apsarasaścātra ye ca puṇyakṛto narāḥ

plain_english: Those who died in these circumstances are situated in the electric level.
sanskrit_cite: bhṛgau vahnau jale ye ca saṃgrāme cānivartinaḥ gograhe vadhyamokṣe vā mṛtāste vaidyute sthitāḥ

plain_english: After the electric level come nourishment clouds, disease-water clouds, and samvartas.
sanskrit_cite: vaidyutādraivatastāvāṃstatra puṣṭivahāmbudāḥ ūrdhvaṃ ca rogāmbumucaḥ saṃvartāstadanantare

plain_english: In raivata there is a place for anger-water releasers, and visavarta is that wind.
sanskrit_cite: rocanāñjanabhasmādisiddhāstatraiva raivate krodhodakamucāṃ sthānaṃ viṣāvartaḥ sa mārutaḥ

plain_english: Fifty above are storm clouds and fire-born vidyadhara specialists who worship the supreme lord.
sanskrit_cite: pañcāśadūrdhvaṃ tatraiva durdinābdā hutāśajāḥ vidyādharaviśeṣāśca tathā ye parameśvaram

plain_english: A hundred above visavarta is durjaya, the breath-born.
sanskrit_cite: gāndharveṇa sadārcanti viṣāvarte@tha te sthitāḥ viṣāvartācchatādūrdhva durjayaḥ śvāsasaṃbhavaḥ

plain_english: Paravaha contains brahma clouds, pushkara clouds, wind-goers, and gandharvas.
sanskrit_cite: brahmaṇo@tra sthitā meghāḥ pralaye vātakāriṇaḥ puṣkarābdā vāyugamā gandharvāśca parāvahe

plain_english: Avaha contains jimuta clouds, highest vidyadharas, and form-vow worlds.
sanskrit_cite: jīmūtameghāstatsaṃjñāstathā vidyādharottamāḥ ye ca rūpavratā lokā āvahe te pratiṣṭhitāḥ

plain_english: Mahavaha has beings-benefiting clouds, and mahaparivaha has skull-born clouds of mahesha.
sanskrit_cite: mahāvahe tvīśakṛtāḥ prajāhitakarāmbudāḥ mahāparivahe meghāḥ kapālotthā maheśituḥ

plain_english: At the end of mahaparivaha is ritarddhi, with eastern wind path, fire daughters, and mothers established by rudra power.
sanskrit_cite: mahāparivahānto@yamṛtarddheḥ prāṅmarutpathaḥ agnikanyā mātaraśca rudraśaktyā tvadhiṣṭhitāḥ

plain_english: The second level has siddhas and caranas, the fourth has divine weapons and direction elephants, and the fifth is noted.
sanskrit_cite: dvitīye tatpare siddhacāraṇā nijakarmajāḥ turye devāyudhānyaṣṭau diggajāḥ pañcame punaḥ

plain_english: The sixth level has garuda, bull, and lord, with daksha; the ninth is established by brahma power.
sanskrit_cite: ṣaṣṭhe garutmānanyasmiṅgaṅgānyatra vṛṣo vibhuḥ dakṣastu navame brahmaśaktyā samadhiti[ni]ṣṭhitaḥ

plain_english: The tenth wind path contains vasus, rudras, and adityas, and the sun's orb is nine thousand yojanas.
sanskrit_cite: daśame vasavo rudrā ādityāśca marutpathe navayojanasāhasro vigraho@rkasya maṇḍalam

plain_english: Svarga loka is defined from bhuvarloka to the end of dhruva, with knowledge power shining as the lord's sun.
sanskrit_cite: triguṇaṃ jñānaśaktiḥ sā tapatyarkatayā prabhoḥ svarlokastu bhuvarlokāddhruvāntaṃ paribhāṣyate

plain_english: Cool-rayed action power of shiva is a lakh from the sun, stellar is a lakh from the moon, then two lakhs.
sanskrit_cite: sūryāllakṣeṇa śītāṃśuḥ kriyāśaktiḥ śivasya sā candrāllakṣeṇa nākṣatraṃ tato lakṣadvayena tu

plain_english: From the earth up to Saturn, the wise know a set of five planets, each at its own interval. From the sun, the realm of the Seven Sages is one lakh away, and from there the Pole Star is placed at the same distance.
sanskrit_cite: pratyekaṃ bhaumataḥ sūryasutānte pañcakaṃ viduḥ saurāllakṣeṇa saptarṣivargastasmāddhruvastathā

plain_english: The unmoving Pole Star is Brahma himself in a lower form, stationed in Brahma's place. It has become the central pivot of all celestial cars and stands above them all.
sanskrit_cite: brahmaivāpararūpeṇa brahmasthāne dhruvo@calaḥ medhībhūto vimānānāṃ sarveṣāmupari dhruvaḥ

plain_english: Here, all things are understood to be bound within the sphere of wind. There are seven heavenly wind masses, chiefly beginning with the clouds and the like.
sanskrit_cite: atra baddhāni sarvāṇyapyūhyante@nilamaṇḍale svassapta mārutaskandhā āmeghādyāḥ pradhānataḥ

plain_english: Those who perform sacrifices and other rites but lack knowledge go to heaven. When that merit is exhausted, they return to the human world because of the merit that still remains.
sanskrit_cite: itaśca kratuhotrādi kṛtvā jñānavivarjitāḥ svaryānti tatkṣaye lokaṃ mānuṣyaṃ puṇyaśeṣataḥ

plain_english: Thus, from the earth up to the Pole Star the distance is fifteen lakhs. From heaven up to the Great World it is two crores and eighty-five lakhs.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ bhūmerdhruvāntaṃ syāllakṣāṇi daśa pañca ca dve koṭī pañca cāśītirlakṣāṇi svargato mahān

plain_english: In the Great World dwell seers, sages, and perfected beings such as Markandeya. Gods whose duties have come to an end also abide there.
sanskrit_cite: mārkaṇḍādyā ṛṣimunisiddhāstatra pratiṣṭhitāḥ nivartitādhikārāśca devā mahati saṃsthitāḥ

plain_english: In the great intermediate space there are others who still hold office. Eight crores above the Great World is the Jana world, where Kapila and others dwell.
sanskrit_cite: mahāntarāle tatrānye tvadhikārabhujo janāḥ aṣṭau koṭyo mahallokājjano@tra kapilādayaḥ

plain_english: Many happy Sadhyas dwell there as well. One crore above the Jana world is the Tapas world, where Sanaka and others of great wisdom reside.
sanskrit_cite: tiṣṭhanti sādhyāstatraiva bahavaḥ sukhabhāginaḥ janāttaporkakoṭyo@tra sanakādyā mahādhiyaḥ

plain_english: There the lords of creatures born from Brahma hold their office. Above the Tapas world, sixteen crores away, is Satya, the abode of Brahma.
sanskrit_cite: prajāpatīnāṃ tatrādhikāro brahmātmajanmanām brahmālayastu tapasaḥ satyaḥ ṣoḍaśa koṭayaḥ

plain_english: There the self-born Brahma dwells and manifests this universe. In the Satya world are the Vedas and others who have been refined by action and meditation.
sanskrit_cite: tatra sthitaḥ sa svayambhūrviśvamāviṣkarotyadaḥ satye vedāstathā cānye karmadhyānena bhāvitāḥ

plain_english: There, above, one crore higher, are those established in bliss at Brahma's seat. Two crores above Brahma's seat is the city of Vishnu.
sanskrit_cite: ānandaniṣṭhāstatrordhvekoṭirvairiñcamāsanam brahmāsanātkoṭiyugmaṃ puraṃ viṣṇornirūpitam

plain_english: Devotees of Vishnu reach that abode through meditation, worship, and recitation. Seven crores above Vishnu's world is the world of the supreme lord.
sanskrit_cite: dhyānapūjājapairviṣṇorbhaktā gacchanti tatpadam vaiṣṇavātsaptakoṭībhirbhuvanaṃ parameśituḥ

plain_english: Rudra is the maker of creation and dissolution within the cosmic egg. Those who are devoted to worship of the linga but lack initiation and knowledge are connected with his realm.
sanskrit_cite: rudrasya sṛṣṭisaṃhārakarturbrahmāṇḍavartmani dīkṣājñānavihīnā ye liṅgārādhanatatparāḥ

plain_english: They go to Rudra's city within the cosmic egg and never fall back down. All who dwell there eventually go to Shiva, becoming Rudras initiated by Srikantha.
sanskrit_cite: te yāntyaṇḍāntare raudraṃ puraṃ nādhaḥ kadācana tatsthāḥ sarve śivaṃ yānti rudrāḥ śrīkaṇṭhadīkṣitāḥ

plain_english: When their office comes to an end, they ascend together with the group of Rudra's daughters, going from city to city above Rudra in ever higher stages.
sanskrit_cite: adhikārakṣaye sākaṃ rudrakanyāgaṇena te puraṃ puraṃ ca rudrordhvamuttarottaravṛddhitaḥ

plain_english: Below the cosmic egg and above Rudra is the city of the staff-bearer. By Shiva's will he holds the egg firm and also opens the path of liberation.
sanskrit_cite: brahmāṇḍādhaśca rudrordhva daṇḍapāṇeḥ puraṃ sa ca śivecchayā dṛṇātyaṇḍaṃ mokṣamārga karoti ca

plain_english: Sharva, Rudra, Bhima, Bhava, Ugra, the great lord, and Ishana are the seven Shiva-lords of the worlds, ruling upward from the earth world.
sanskrit_cite: śarvarudrau bhīmabhavāvugro devo mahānatha īśāna iti bhūrlokāt sapta lokeśvarāḥ śivāḥ

plain_english: Seven worlds are formed from gross particulars, while the higher worlds are formed from subtle ones. The teacher explained this clearly in the Ruru scripture.
sanskrit_cite: sthūlairviśeṣairārabdhāḥ sapta lokāḥ pare punaḥ sūkṣmairiti guruścaiva rurau samyaṅnyarūpayat

plain_english: In Brahma's first creation, five gross particulars called the abundant ones were made from his own body. With a seventh formed from them, these became the basis of the seven worlds.
sanskrit_cite: ye brahmaṇādisarge svaśarīrānnirmitāḥ prabhūtākhyāḥ sthūlāḥ pañca viśeṣāḥ saptāmī tanmayā lokāḥ

plain_english: Beyond that, the worlds are supported by subtle coverings: great elements born from the tanmatras, upheld through subtle bodies and mutually connected by smell and the other subtle qualities.
sanskrit_cite: parato liṅgādhāraiḥ sūkṣmaistanmātrajairmahābhūtaiḥ lokānāmāvaraṇairviṣṭabhya parasperaṇa gandhādyaiḥ

plain_english: From the fire of time up to the staff-bearer the distance is eighty-eight crores. Above that, within the cosmic egg, is a solid shell one crore yojanas thick.
sanskrit_cite: kālāgnerdaṇḍapāṇyantamaṣṭānavatikoṭayaḥ ata ūrdhvaṃ kaṭāho@ṇḍe sa ghanaḥ koṭiyojanam

plain_english: There are fifty crores above the earth's surface and fifty crores below, making the earth sphere one hundred crores in all. From that it is pictured like a golden grain of rice.
sanskrit_cite: pañcāśatkoṭayaścordhvaṃ bhūpṛṣṭhādadharaṃ tathā evaṃ koṭiśataṃ bhūḥ syāt sauvarṇastaṇḍulastataḥ

plain_english: The mantra extending to the hundred Rudras, with the syllables hum and phat, splits that hard-to-pacify boundary. Ten by ten in every direction, there are a hundred Rudras outside.
sanskrit_cite: śatarudrāvadhirhuphaṭ bhedayettattu duḥśamam pratidikkaṃ daśa daśetyevaṃ rudraśataṃ bahiḥ

plain_english: That which supports the cosmic egg does so by its own power on all sides. The teachers, in the Raurava and other scriptures, have said that it has the form of an egg.
sanskrit_cite: brahmāṇḍādhārakaṃ tacca svaprabhāveṇa sarvataḥ aṇḍasvarūpaṃ gurubhiścoktaṃ śrīrauravādiṣu

plain_english: The cosmic egg is the mass of reality that has turned toward manifestation, emerged from the form of power, and remains undivided by any addition or removal.
sanskrit_cite: vyakterabhimukhībhūtaḥ pracyutaḥ śaktirūpataḥ āvāpavānanirbhakto vastupiṇḍo@ṇḍa ucyate

plain_english: The upper shell of the egg is sattva mixed with a trace of darkness, while the lower shell is sattva mixed with activity and associated with darkness.
sanskrit_cite: tamoleśānuviddhasya kapālaṃ sattvamuttaram rajo@nuviddhaṃ nirmṛṣṭaṃ sattvamasyādharaṃ tamaḥ

plain_english: The mass of reality is said to partake of the collectivity of Shiva and Shakti, and because it turns toward manifestation it is called an egg.
sanskrit_cite: vastupiṇḍa iti proktaṃ śivaśaktisamūhabhāk aṇḍaḥ syāditi tadvyaktau saṃmukhībhāva ucyate

plain_english: One might object that powers immersed in Shiva should also be eggs, but they are not, because they have not fallen from their own state of power.
sanskrit_cite: tathāpi śivamagnānāṃ śaktīnāmaṇḍatā bhavet tadartha vākyamaparaṃ tā hi na cyutaśaktitaḥ

plain_english: Another clarifying term is used so that egg-ness is not wrongly extended to bodies and sense bases, because nothing is inserted into them in that way.
sanskrit_cite: tanvakṣādau mā prasāṅkṣīdaṇḍateti padāntaram tanvakṣādiṣu naivāste kasyāpyāvāpanaṃ yataḥ

plain_english: If bodies and sense bases form a collectivity, their oneness is explained by the word 'undivided', which shows that they share the same kind.
sanskrit_cite: tanvakṣasamudāyatve kathamekatvamityataḥ anirbhakta iti proktaṃ sājātyaparidarśakam

plain_english: Someone might think that, even without using the term 'mass of reality', each principle by itself could have the nature of an egg; but the text challenges that idea.
sanskrit_cite: vināpi vastupiṇḍākhyapadenaikaikaśo bhavet tattveṣvaṇḍasvabhāvatvaṃ nanvevamapi kiṃ na tat

plain_english: Egg-nature would wrongly extend to a principle made only of qualities, subtle elements, and gross elements; but the word 'reality' here means the whole made of bodies, sense bases, and worlds.
sanskrit_cite: guṇatanmātrabhūtaughamaye tattve prasajyate ucyate vastuśabdena tanvakṣabhuvanātmakam

plain_english: Because that form has already been defined, its collectivity is called an egg; and this collectivity belongs to the Lord who bears the universe as his body.
sanskrit_cite: rūpamuktaṃ yatastena tatsamūho@ṇḍa ucyate bhavecca tatsamūhatvaṃ patyurviśvavapurbhṛtaḥ

plain_english: For that reason, other distinguishing terms were introduced, to show that egg-ness applies only within the limited states of the path-sphere that depends on Maya.
sanskrit_cite: tadartha bhedakānyanyānyupāttānīti darśitam tāvanmātrāsvavasthāsu māyādhīne@dhvamaṇḍale

plain_english: Others say the distinguishing terms were used to prevent egg-ness from being misapplied; in any case, beyond the Brahma egg described here there are one hundred Rudras.
sanskrit_cite: mā bhūdaṇḍatvamityāhuranye bhedakayojanam itthamuktaviriñcāṇḍamṛto rudrāḥ śataṃ hi yat

plain_english: Over those hundred Rudras stand eleven radiant Rudra-lords of their own: Ananta, Kapalin, Agni, Yama, Nairrita, Bala, and the rest named in sequence.
sanskrit_cite: teṣāṃ sve patayo rudrā ekādaśa mahārciṣaḥ ananto@tha kapālyāgniryamanairṛtakau balaḥ

plain_english: The remaining Rudra-lords are Shighra, Nidhisha, Vidyesha, Shambhu, and Virabhadra; they surround the Brahma egg like bees covering honey and clusters of kadamba filaments.
sanskrit_cite: śīghro nidhīśo vidyeśaḥ śambhuḥ savīrabhadrakaḥ madhu madhukṛtaḥ kadambaṃ kesarajālāni yadvadāvṛṇate

plain_english: In the same way, the Shiva-Rudras, with countless attendants, surround the Brahma egg; their arrangement is described in vast numbers, such as forty niyutas and a crore.
sanskrit_cite: tadvatte śivarudrā brahmāṇḍamasaṃkhyaparivārāḥ śarāṣṭaniyutaṃ koṭirityeṣāṃ sanniveśanam

plain_english: Presided over by Shrikantha, these Rudras create and withdraw, and they hold lordship over the gods, as stated in the Raurava Vartika.
sanskrit_cite: śrīkaṇṭhādhiṣṭhitāste ca sṛjanti saṃharanti ca īśvaratvaṃ diviṣadāmiti rauravavārtike

plain_english: But in the Siddha Tantra, beyond a hundred crores from the golden egg, there is a sequence of a hundred more eggs, successively doubled and associated with silver and other substances.
sanskrit_cite: siddhātantre tu hemāṇḍācchatakoṭerbahiḥ śatam aṇḍānāṃ kramaśo dvidviguṇaṃ rūpyādiyojitam

plain_english: In those eggs, Brahmas exist in sequence with doubled lifespans; they perish in order, and at the end of that series a higher principle is reached.
sanskrit_cite: teṣu krameṇa brahmāṇaḥ saṃsyurdviguṇajīvitāḥ kṣīyante kramaśaste ca tadante tattvamammayam

plain_english: From earth upward come water and the rest in order; up to ego the scale increases tenfold, and beyond that intellect increases a hundredfold.
sanskrit_cite: dharāto@tra jalādi syāduttarottarataḥ kramāt daśadhāhaṅkṛtāntaṃ dhīstasyāḥ syācchatadhā tataḥ

plain_english: Above intellect, manifest nature is a thousandfold, purusha is ten thousandfold, and niyati is a hundred thousandfold, leading to a millionfold beyond it.
sanskrit_cite: sahasradhā vyaktamataḥ pauṃsnaṃ daśasahasradhā niyatirlakṣadhā tasmāttasyāstu daśalakṣadhā

plain_english: Up to kala the scale is ten millionfold, Maya is a hundred millionfold, Ishvara is a billionfold, and beyond that it reaches a thousand crores.
sanskrit_cite: kalāntaṃ koṭidhā tasmānmāyā viddaśakoṭidhā īśvaraḥ śatakoṭiḥ syāttasmātkoṭisahasradhā

plain_english: Sadakhya pervades at that vast scale, and together with its multitude of powers the all-pervading goddess is established as pervading the entire path.
sanskrit_cite: sādākhyaṃ vyaśnute tacca śaktirvṛndena saṃkhyayā vyāpinī sarvamadhvānaṃ vyāpyadevī vyavasthitā

plain_english: Beyond all that is the pure, supreme, immeasurable Shiva principle; from water up to Shiva-tattva, no one but Shiva has truly seen it.
sanskrit_cite: aprameyaṃ tataḥ śuddhaṃ śivatattvaṃ paraṃ viduḥ jalādeḥ śivatattvāntaṃ na dṛṣṭaṃ kenacicchivāt

plain_english: For that reason, knowledge of Shiva is the supreme cause of liberation, as Mahadeva declares in the revered Svacchanda scripture.
sanskrit_cite: ṛte tataḥ śivajñānaṃ paramaṃ mokṣakāraṇam tathā cāha mahādevaḥ śrīmatsvacchandaśāsane

plain_english: A bound soul does not attain liberation by hundreds of other kinds of knowledge; knowledge of Shiva does not arise without receiving Shaiva initiation.
sanskrit_cite: nānyathā mokṣamāyāti paśurjñānaśatairapi śivajñānaṃ na bhavati dīkṣāmaprāpya śāṅkarīm

plain_english: The former supreme power, and the human-made one too, again grants blue-radiant victory above the hundred rudras, associated with Bhadrakali.
sanskrit_cite: prāktanī pārameśī sā pauruṣeyī ca sā punaḥ śatarudrordhvato bhadrakālyā nīlaprabhaṃ jayam

plain_english: Kali's victorious city is not attainable by sacrifice, gift, or austerity; her devotees, well initiated in her circle, go there.
sanskrit_cite: na yajñadānatapasā prāpyaṃ kālyāḥ puraṃ jayam tadbhaktāstatra gacchanti tanmaṇḍalasudīkṣitāḥ

plain_english: The supreme goddess gives liberation through seedless initiation; she performs for people as much initiation as corresponds to the vidyesha veil.
sanskrit_cite: nirbījadīkṣayā mokṣaṃ dadāti parameśvarī vidyeśāvaraṇe dīkṣāṃ yāvatīṃ kurute nṛṇām

plain_english: Those placed in this world attain a corresponding state; then Virabhadra, shining like end-of-age fire, appears by crores.
sanskrit_cite: tāvatīṃ gatimāyānti bhuvane@tra niveśitāḥ tataḥ koṭyā vīrabhadro yugāntāgnisamaprabhaḥ

plain_english: Those who remember the great lord and die in water, desert, fire, or by beheading reach his city called Vijaya.
sanskrit_cite: vijayākhyaṃ puraṃ cāsya ye smaranto maheśvaram jaleṣu maruṣu cāgnau śiraśchedena vā mṛtāḥ

plain_english: They go to knowledge-Ishana and radiant Virabhadra, in a region spread by crores above Virabhadra, in three ways.
sanskrit_cite: te yānti bodhamaiśānaṃ vīrabhadraṃ mahādyutim vairabhadrordhvataḥ koṭirviṣkambhādvistṛtaṃ tridhā

plain_english: The water-bearing rudra egg, bow-shaped, is situated from Virabhadra's world and likewise from Bhadrakali's abode.
sanskrit_cite: rudrāṇḍaṃ sālilaṃ tvaṇḍaṃ śakracāpākṛti sthitam ā vīrabhadrabhuvanādbhadrakālyālayāttathā

plain_english: Adorned by thirteen other worlds, then earth with its mountain is defined by holding the smell tanmatra.
sanskrit_cite: trayodaśabhiranyaiśca bhuvanairupaśobhitam tato bhuvaḥ sahādreḥ pūrgandhatanmātradhāraṇāt

plain_english: The dead go to that supreme earth; the wise go to the ocean city, attainable by holding the taste tanmatra.
sanskrit_cite: mṛtā gacchanti tāṃ bhūmiṃ dharitryāḥ paramāṃ budhāḥ abdheḥ puraṃ tatastvāpyaṃ rasatanmātradhāraṇāt

plain_english: Then Shri's city is reached in Rudra's play descents, especially by special death at Prayaga and Shri mountain.
sanskrit_cite: tataḥ śriyaḥ puraṃ rudrakrīḍāvataraṇeṣvatha prayāgādau śrīgirau ca viśeṣānmaraṇena tat

plain_english: Sarasvati city is the abode of knowers of sound-Brahman; those suitable to Rudra are situated there, while others stand apart from Rudras due to primacy.
sanskrit_cite: sārasvataṃ puraṃ tasmācchabdabrahmavidāṃ padam rudrocitāstā mukhyatvādrudrebhyo@nyāstathā sthitāḥ

plain_english: In many cities Ganga, Shri, and Sarasvati appear; god-lords range from Lakula to Amarasha, with eight in the waters.
sanskrit_cite: pureṣu bahudhā gaṅgā devādau śrīḥ sarasvatī lakulādyamareśāntā aṣṭāvapsu surādhipāḥ

plain_english: Then the fiery principle is the abode of Shiva-fire here; those who have resorted to fiery holding go to this fire.
sanskrit_cite: tatastu taijasaṃ tattvaṃ śivāgneratra saṃsthitiḥ te cainaṃ vahnimāyānti vāhnīṃ ye dhāraṇāṃ śritāḥ

plain_english: In the fiery principle there are eight leaders from Bhairava to Hari; breath has a world, and air is divided in ten ways.
sanskrit_cite: bhairavādiharīndvantaṃ taijase nāyakāṣṭakam prāṇasya bhuvanaṃ vāyordaśadhā daśadhā tu tat

plain_english: Having meditated or abandoned breaths and made holding there, great souls enter that, becoming air and sky-bodied.
sanskrit_cite: dhyātvā tyaktvātha vā prāṇān kṛtvā tatraiva dhāraṇām taṃ viśanti mahātmāno vāyubhūtāḥ khamūrtayaḥ

plain_english: The eight from Bhima to Gaya go to the air principle; the sky world is attainable by holding that space.
sanskrit_cite: bhīmādigayaparyantamaṣṭakaṃ vāyutattvagam khatattve bhuvanaṃ vyomnaḥ prāpyaṃ tadvyomadhāraṇāt

plain_english: From cloth-foot-end to pillar-etc and eight gods are in the space principle; uninitiated beings claiming the Shiva principle are among beings.
sanskrit_cite: vastrāpadāntaṃ sthāṇvādi vyomatattve surāṣṭakam adīkṣitā ye bhūteṣu śivatattvābhimāninaḥ

plain_english: Even those lacking knowledge, despite strong holding, go outside from the egg; earth, ocean, fire, air, and space goers, and initiated ones too, are named.
sanskrit_cite: jñānahīnā api prauḍhadhāraṇāste@ṇḍato bahiḥ dharābdhitejo@nilakhapuragā dīkṣitāśca vā

plain_english: For the purpose of purification yoga, the supreme state is not sought in such descents, even for those who die in shrines.
sanskrit_cite: tāvatsaṃskārayogārthaṃ na paraṃ padamīhitum tathāvidhāvatāreṣu mṛtāścāyataneṣu ye

plain_english: Having attained that state, they gradually go to Shiva-nature; this is said again in the Shrimad Devi Tantra.
sanskrit_cite: tatpadaṃ te samāsādya kramādyānti śivātmatām punaḥ punaridaṃ coktaṃ śrīmaddevyākhyayāmale

plain_english: In the Shri Kamika's Kashmir description the lord has said that those who die in the great abode of the goddess die in that city.
sanskrit_cite: śrīkāmikāyāṃ kaśmīravarṇane coktavānvibhuḥ sureśvarīmahādhāmni ye mriyante ca tatpure

plain_english: Brahmins and mixed castes, beings up to immobile forms, and Rudra classes are these; thus says Lord Shiva.
sanskrit_cite: brāhmaṇādyāḥ saṅkarāntāḥ paśavaḥ sthāvarāntagāḥ rudrajātaya evaite ityāha bhagavāñchivaḥ

plain_english: Dear one, the cities of tanmatras through mind lie above the sky veil and below ego, in Shiva's doctrine.
sanskrit_cite: ākāśāvaraṇādūrdhvamahaṅkārādadhaḥ priye tanmātrādimano@ntānāṃ purāṇi śivaśāsane

plain_english: The great smell-tanmatra circle, joined with five colors, is situated between, covered by many crores of yojanas.
sanskrit_cite: pañcavarṇayutaṃ gandhatanmātramaṇḍalaṃ mahat ācchādya yojanānekakoṭibhiḥ sthitamantarā

plain_english: Thus the circles of measures beginning with essence, each by its own color, are Śarva, Bhava, Paśupati, Īśa, and Bhīma in order.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ rasādimātrāṇāṃ maṇḍalāni svavarṇata śarvo bhavaḥ paśupatirīśo bhīma iti kramāt

plain_english: The lords of the tanmatras—sound and the rest—are the makers of space and the other elements; by whose will they act, from that arise the spheres of the sun, moon, and Vedas, through the great all-pervading one.
sanskrit_cite: tanmātreśā yadicchātaḥ śabdādyāḥ khādikāriṇaḥ tataḥ sūryenduvedānāṃ maṇḍalāni vibhurmahān

plain_english: Among these, ugra and the rest; lords from them, sun and moon; together with sacrificers—thus eight supreme forms of Śambhu are declared.
sanskrit_cite: ugraścetyeṣu patayastebhyo@rkendū sayājakau ityaṣṭau tanavaḥ śaṃbhoryāḥ parāḥ parikīrtitāḥ

plain_english: The other worlds in Brahma's egg, having pervaded all, are situated; in each eon they are indeed produced from earth and the rest.
sanskrit_cite: aparā brahmaṇo@ṇḍe tā vyāpya sarvaṃ vyavasthitāḥ kalpe kalpe prasūyante dharādyāstābhya eva tu

plain_english: Then the group of organs, joined with the speech and action senses, has Agni, Indra, Viṣṇu, and Mitra as leaders, with Brahmā among them.
sanskrit_cite: tato vāgādikarmākṣayuktaṃ karaṇamaṇḍalam agnīndraviṣṇumitrāḥ sabrahmāṇasteṣu nāyakāḥ

plain_english: From that heard light-circle, the intellect and the five senses have as their deities directions, lightning, sun, Varuṇa, and earths; ear and the rest likewise.
sanskrit_cite: prakāśamaṇḍalaṃ tasmācchrutaṃ buddhyakṣapañcakam digvidyudarkavaruṇabhuvaḥ śrotrādidevatāḥ

plain_english: Above the sphere of light is situated the sphere of the five objects; from this, the sphere of mind is presided over by Soma, because...
sanskrit_cite: prakāśamaṇḍalādūrdhvaṃ sthitaṃ pañcārthamaṇḍalam manomaṇḍalametasmāt somenādhiṣṭhitaṃ yataḥ

plain_english: Presiding over the external gods, whose nature is equality, sovereignty, and bliss, the mind-god is then declared to be the divine, all-pervading Soma.
sanskrit_cite: bāhyadeveṣvadhiṣṭhātā sāmyaiśvaryasukhātmakaḥ manodevastato divyaḥ somo vibhurudīritaḥ

plain_english: Then also, the world-city of the ego-principle is joined with all sense-organs, arising from the source born of intellect-senses, together with eight from gross to goat.
sanskrit_cite: tato@pi sakalākṣāṇāṃ yonerbuddhyakṣajanmanaḥ sthūlādicchagalāntāṣṭayuktaṃ cāhaṅkṛteḥ puram

plain_english: The buddhi-principle; then the lord of the eight divine-womb cities, from paiśāca up to brāhma, is declared.
sanskrit_cite: buddhitattvaṃ tato devayonyaṣṭakapurādhipam paiśācaprabhṛtibrāhmaparyantaṃ tacca kīrtitam

plain_english: These are indeed the ancient abodes of the divine wombs; having descended and meditated on their own birth, they arise.
sanskrit_cite: etāni devayonīnāṃ sthānānyeva purāṇyataḥ avatīryātmajanmānaṃ dhyāyantaḥ saṃbhavanti te

plain_english: By the command of the supreme lord, beings are impelled by māyā and regulated by niyati, in connection with Brahmā's unmanifest birth.
sanskrit_cite: parameśaniyogācca codyamānāśca māyayā niyāmitā niyatyā ca brahmaṇo@vyaktajanmanaḥ

plain_english: Therefore, at the beginning of creation, the great beings are manifested in many names and forms through their own aspect, yet they do not abandon their own abode.
sanskrit_cite: vyajyante tena sargādau nāmarūpairanekadhā svāṃśanaiva mahātmāno na tyajanti svaketanam

plain_english: And it was said to us by a teacher established in authority and knowing the Shiva doctrine that these are indeed the wombs of manifestation of power for the eight gods.
sanskrit_cite: uktaṃ ca śivatanāvidamadhikārapadasthitena guruṇā naḥ aṣṭānāṃ devānāṃ śaktyāvirbhāvayonayo hyetāḥ

plain_english: Below these, their bodily enjoyments are declared to be abundant, and there are forty worlds with corresponding regions of equal enjoyment.
sanskrit_cite: tanubhogāḥ punareṣāmadhaḥ prabhūtātmakāḥ proktāḥ catvāriṃśattulyopabhogadeśādhikāni bhuvanāni

plain_english: These are described only as groups of eight and five because of differences in means, and they are reached through devotion, yoga, the giving up of life, and so forth.
sanskrit_cite: sādhanabhedātkevalamaṣṭakapañcakatayoktāni etāni bhaktiyogaprāṇatyāgādigamyāni

plain_english: Among these, Umapati alone is the lord, possessing independent senses yet being without organs; from him, by gradation, the octad of divine wombs is to be recognized.
sanskrit_cite: teṣūmāpatireva prabhuḥ svatantrendriyo vikaraṇātmā taratamayogena tato@pi devayonyaṣṭakaṃ lakṣyaṃ tu

plain_english: The senses of the worlds are instruments that delimit objects; through a sequence increasing by one from smell up to mahat, sovereignty arises.
sanskrit_cite: lokānāmakṣāṇi ca viṣayaparicchittikaraṇāni gandhādermahadantādekādhikyena jātamaiśvaryam

plain_english: Knowing thus that powers like anima operate in this range from the paisaca level up to Virinca, one should purify the intellect together with the eight constituents of the subtle city and the senses.
sanskrit_cite: aṇimādyātmakamasminpaiśācādye viriñcānte jñātvaivaṃ śodhayedbuddhiṃ sārdhaṃ puryaṣṭakendriyaiḥ

plain_english: They know the octad of Krodhesas, beginning with Samvarta and led by Anila, and then the octad of fires arising from the wrathful octad beginning with Baladhyaksa.
sanskrit_cite: krodheśāṣṭakamānīlaṃ saṃvartādyaṃ tato viduḥ tejoṣṭakaṃ balādhyakṣaprabhṛtikrodhanāṣtakāt

plain_english: Then the octad of yogas beginning with Akrta is declared in the intellect in the Svacchanda teaching, but in the teaching beginning with Sri it is placed in the root.
sanskrit_cite: akṛtādi tato buddhau yogāṣṭakamudāhṛtam svacchandaśāsane tattu mūle śrīpūrvaśāsane

plain_english: At the level of the yoga octad, in Soma, there is what belongs to Srikantha; then comes the city of Maya, which is again spoken of as belonging to Srikantha.
sanskrit_cite: yogāṣṭakapade yattu some śraikaṇṭhameva ca tato māyāpuraṃ bhūyaḥ śrīkaṇṭhasya ca kathyate

plain_english: Therefore, a second world is spoken of separately for those two; there, in the city of Maya, the universe is presided over by a goddess.
sanskrit_cite: tena dvitīyaṃ bhuvanaṃ tayoḥ pratyekamucyate tatra māyāpuraṃ devyā yayā viśvamadhiṣṭhitam

plain_english: In each cosmic age that great goddess is described by different names; the city of the lord of Uma is then surrounded by the Mothers.
sanskrit_cite: pratikalpaṃ nāmabhedairbhaṇyate sā maheśvarī umāpateḥ puraṃ paścānmātṛbhiḥ parivāritam

plain_english: Shrikantha is the supreme form, and attendant goddesses such as Brahmi, Skandaja, Hari, Varahi, Indri, Viccika, and Carcika are named.
sanskrit_cite: śrīkaṇṭha eva parayā mūrtyomāpatirucyate brāhmyaiśī skandajā hārī vārāhyaindrī saviccikā [carcikā]

plain_english: Yellow, white, yellow-blue, blue, and white-red are assigned in order to the corresponding directional goddesses.
sanskrit_cite: pītā śuklā pītanīle nīlā śuklāruṇā kramāt agnīśasaumyayāmyāpyapūrvanairṛtagāstu tāḥ

plain_english: By portion, the creator descends some goddesses into the human world, while other supreme ones remain established in the sky.
sanskrit_cite: aṃśena mānuṣe loke dhātrā tā hyavatāritāḥ svacchandāstāḥ parāścānyāḥ pare vyomni vyavasthitāḥ

plain_english: Those goddesses serve self-willed, because above the city of Uma's lord stands the supreme eight-fold form.
sanskrit_cite: svacchandaṃ tā niṣevante saptadheyamumā yataḥ umāpatipurasyordhva sthitaṃ mūrtyaṣṭakaṃ param

plain_english: From those whose creation begins with Sharva and earth, the Ishana form is established on Meru.
sanskrit_cite: śarvādikaṃ yasya sṛṣṭirdharādyā yājakāntataḥ tābhya īśānamūrtiryā sā merau saṃpratiṣṭhitā

plain_english: Shrikantha pervades the world through eight bodies, and restrained devotees worship Shambhu's qualified yoga.
sanskrit_cite: śrīkaṇṭhaḥ sphaṭikādrau sā vyāptā tanvaṣṭakairjagat ye yogaṃ saguṇaṃ śambhoḥ saṃyatāḥ paryupāsate

plain_english: By seeing that circle, one is freed from duality, the three are removed, and the gunas are established in purity and impurity.
sanskrit_cite: tanmaṇḍalaṃ vā dṛṣṭvaiva muktadvaitā hṛtatrayāḥ guṇānāmādharauttaryācchuddhāśuddhatvasaṃsthiteḥ

plain_english: Because of gradation and difference in yoga, the fruits are varied, and this difference is called difference in enjoyment and attainment.
sanskrit_cite: tāratamyācca yogasya bhedātphalavicitratā tato bhogaphalāvāptibhedādbhedo@yamucyate

plain_english: Above the eight forms, twelve radiant saffron forms are declared, ranging from Vama to Eka Shiva.
sanskrit_cite: mūrtyaṣṭakopariṣṭāttu suśivā dvādaśoditāḥ vāmādyekaśivāntāste kuṅkumābhāḥ sutejasaḥ

plain_english: Above that stands Virabhadra, lord of the circle; one who attains sayujya delights together with him.
sanskrit_cite: tadūrdhva vīrabhadrākhyo maṇḍalādhipatiḥ sthitaḥ yatta [sta] tsāyujyamāpannaḥ sa tena saha modate

plain_english: From the eight divine wombs to the thumb-sized end, eight Mahadevas may be, and this intellect principle is declared.
sanskrit_cite: tato@pyaṅguṣṭhamātrāntaṃ mahādevāṣṭakaṃ bhavet buddhitattvamidaṃ proktaṃ devayonyaṣṭakāditaḥ

plain_english: At the end of the eight Mahadevas, the eight yoga is declared here; there Shrikantha, lord of Uma, is declared.
sanskrit_cite: mahādevāṣṭakānte tad yogāṣṭakamihoditam tatra śraikaṇṭhamuktaṃ yat tasyaivomāpatistathā

plain_english: Auspicious forms, the hero, the eight Mahadevas, and the body are named; nature's gunas are above and below intellect.
sanskrit_cite: mūrtayaḥ suśivā vīro mahādevāṣṭakaṃ vapuḥ upariṣṭāddhiyo@dhaśca prakṛterguṇasaṃjñitam

plain_english: There agitated gunas produce intellect; inequality not attained is not a cause for producing effects.
sanskrit_cite: tattvaṃ tatra tu saṃkṣubdhā guṇāḥ prasuvate dhiyam na vaiṣamyamanāpannaṃ kāraṇaṃ kāryasūtaye

plain_english: Nature may be cause through guna equilibrium, but without agitation it still has unequal gunas.
sanskrit_cite: guṇasāmyatmikā tena prakṛtiḥ kāraṇaṃ bhavet nanvevaṃ sāpi saṃkṣobhaṃ vinā tānviṣamānguṇān

plain_english: How would instability arise in the first agitation? This is Sankhya's fault, if by that those gunas.
sanskrit_cite: kathaṃ suvīta tatrādye kṣobhe syādanavasthitiḥ sāṃkhyasya doṣa evāyaṃ yadi vā tena te guṇāḥ

plain_english: The unmanifest is desired; equilibrium is mere contact, not otherwise, and our view joins it with the independent lord's will agitation.
sanskrit_cite: avyaktamiṣṭāḥ sāmyaṃ tu saṅgamātraṃ na cetarat asmākaṃ tu svatantreśatathecchākṣobhasaṃgatam

plain_english: The unmanifest is cause of intellect principle; agitated gunas are involved, and nature's agitation comes from the lord's will before.
sanskrit_cite: avyaktaṃ buddhitattvasya kāraṇaṃ kṣobhitā guṇāḥ nanu tattveśvarecchāto yaḥ kṣobhaḥ prakṛteḥ purā

plain_english: That indeed may be the intellect principle; what need of other imagined gunas? It is not obstructed by cause-form reflection.
sanskrit_cite: tadeva buddhitattvaṃ syāt kimanyaiḥ kalpitairguṇaiḥ naitatkāraṇatārūpaparāmarśāvarodhi yat

plain_english: Then other agitation produces effects like seed and sprout, and rows of heavy ones are established in tamas, rajas, and sattva.
sanskrit_cite: kṣobhāntaraṃ tataḥ kārya bījocchūnāṅkurādivat kramāttamorajaḥsattve gurūṇāṃ paṅktayaḥ sthitāḥ

plain_english: Three, thirty-two, one, thirty-one, and twenty-one are listed; by their own knowledge, yoga, and power, the best teachers play.
sanskrit_cite: tisro dvātriṃśadekātastriṃśadapyekaviṃśatiḥ svajñanayogabalataḥ krīḍanto daiśikottamāḥ

plain_english: Three-eyed ones, freed from bonds, do grace; intellect and guna extend to both, seven more than a hundred.
sanskrit_cite: trinetrāḥ pāśanirmuktāste@trānugrahakāriṇaḥ buddheśca guṇaparyantamubhe saptādhike śate

plain_english: Among Rudras and worlds, chiefly others, the eight yoga is declared between them, in the guna mass and again in Shiva's body.
sanskrit_cite: rudrāṇāṃ bhuvanānāṃ ca mukhyato@nye tadantare yogāṣṭakaṃ guṇaskandhe proktaṃ śivatanau punaḥ

plain_english: Having transcended the womb, in the secondary mass, yoga givers would be unmade, made, vibhu, Virincha, Hari, Guha, and then goddess by order.
sanskrit_cite: yonīratītya gauṇe skandhe syuryogadātāraḥ akṛtakṛtavibhuviriñcā harirguhaḥ kramavaśāttato devī

plain_english: From the unmanifest arise the organs, the subtle powers like smallness, the effects, the manifold of cognitions, and the qualities beginning with sattva.
sanskrit_cite: karaṇānyaṇimādiguṇāḥ kāryāṇi pratyayaprapañcaśca avyaktādutpannā guṇāśca sattvādayo@mīṣām

plain_english: These givers of yoga, arising from the qualities, bestow on souls merit, knowledge, dispassion, lordship, and their various fruits.
sanskrit_cite: dharmajñānavirāgānaiśvaryaṃ tatphalāni vividhāni yacchanti guṇebhyo@mī puruṣebhyo yogadātāraḥ

plain_english: Beyond them is the world of the god Śrīkaṇṭhanātha, who is seated on the qualities beginning with sattva and is the lord and consort of the one mother of the entire universe.
sanskrit_cite: tebhyaḥ parato bhuvanaṃ sattvādiguṇāsanasya devasya sakalajagadekamāturbhartuḥ śrīkaṇṭhanāthasya

plain_english: By his power, taking a seizing form, he presides over the beings in the worlds of Umā, Guha, Nīla, Brahmā, Ṛbhukṣa, Kṛta, Akṛta, and others.
sanskrit_cite: yenomāguhanīlabrahmaṛbhukṣakṛtākṛtādibhuvaneṣu graharūpiṇyā śaktyā prābhvyādhiṣṭhāni bhūtāni

plain_english: When he wishes to withdraw the worlds, he enters the lotus of the four-faced Brahmā, burns the four worlds, and then creates the human worlds again.
sanskrit_cite: upasaṃjihīrṣuriha yaścaturānanapaṅkajaṃ samāviśya dagdhvā caturo lokāñjanalokānnirmiṇoti punaḥ

plain_english: By his will, Rudrāṇī, whose body consists of the qualities beginning with sattva, brings forth in each cycle, and there she is worshiped at the altar in every cycle.
sanskrit_cite: yasyecchātaḥ sattvādiguṇaśarīrā visṛjati rudrāṇī anukalpo rudrāṇyā vedī tatrejyate@nukalpena

plain_english: Then, in connection with that attainment, Paśupati, Indra, Upendra, Viriñci, the gods, and also gandharvas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, ancestors, and sages perform varied sacrifices.
sanskrit_cite: paśupatirindropendraviriñcairatha tadupalambhato devaiḥ gandharvayakṣarākṣasapitṛmunibhiścitritāstathā yāgāḥ

plain_english: The supreme equilibrium of the qualities is the unmanifest. Above the level of the qualities are Krodheśa, Caṇḍa, Saṃvarta, Jyotiḥ, Piṅgala, and Sūraka.
sanskrit_cite: guṇānāṃ yatparaṃ sāmyaṃ tadavyaktaṃ guṇordhvataḥ krodheśacaṇḍasaṃvartā jyotiḥpiṅgalasūrakau

plain_english: There are Pañcāntaka, Ekavīra, and Śikhin, making eight. There that principle is the dense resting place of the soul, prakṛti, the root, pradhāna, the unmanifest.
sanskrit_cite: pañcāntakaikavīrau ca śikhodaścāṣṭa tatra te gahanaṃ puruṣanidhānaṃ prakṛtirmūlaṃ pradhānamavyaktam

plain_english: These are synonymous names for the cause of the qualities, belonging to what arises from māyā; all the embodied knowers whose minds are stained by innate and adventitious impurity are there.
sanskrit_cite: guṇakāraṇamityete māyāprabhavasya paryāyāḥ yāvantaḥ kṣetrajñāḥ sahajāgantukamalopadigdhacitaḥ

plain_english: All of them are established there, along with Rudras who enjoy the experiences arising from it. Some have faculties that are deluded, manifest, or dissolved, while others are without faculties.
sanskrit_cite: te sarve@tra vinihitā rudrāśca tadutthabhogabhujaḥ mūḍhavivṛttavilīnaiḥ karaṇaiḥ kecittu vikaraṇakāḥ

plain_english: In the teaching, faculties that are not yet governed and cannot act are called deluded, while those that clearly grasp their fixed objects are called unfolded.
sanskrit_cite: akṛtādhiṣṭhānatayā kṛtyāśaktāni mūḍhāni pratiniyataviṣayabhāñji sphuṭāni śāstre vivṛttāni

plain_english: At the great dissolution they are broken and dissolved; at creation they are not yet produced. Dependent on will, they are again called without faculties, and the same is true of their effects.
sanskrit_cite: bhagnāni mahāpralaye sṛṣṭau notpāditāni līnāni icchādhīnāni punarvikaraṇasaṃjñāni kāryamapyevam

plain_english: At the level of the puruṣa principle there are the nine satisfactions, the eight accomplishments, and likewise the eight worlds beginning with aṇimā.
sanskrit_cite: puṃstattve tuṣṭinavakaṃ siddhayo@ṣṭau ca tatpuraḥ tāvatya evāṇimādibhuvanāṣṭakameva ca

plain_english: When what is not the true principle is taken as a principle, the resulting contentment is called satisfaction. Taking what should be rejected as acceptable is called accomplishment, as the Kāpilas say.
sanskrit_cite: atattve tattvabuddhyā yaḥ santoṣastuṣṭiratra sā heye@pyādeyadhīḥ siddhiḥ tathā coktaṃ hi kāpilaiḥ

plain_english: Four satisfactions are internal, named prakṛti, acquisition, time, and fortune. Five arise from turning away from objects through gain, protection, association, loss, and obstruction.
sanskrit_cite: ādhyātmikāścatasraḥ prakṛtyupādānakālabhāgyākhyāḥ pañca viṣayoparamato@rjanarakṣāsaṅgasaṃkṣayavighātaiḥ

plain_english: Reasoning, scriptural word, and study are three means that remove suffering; gaining friends and giving are also included, making the eight accomplishments. The obstacle before accomplishment is threefold.
sanskrit_cite: ūhaḥ śabdo@dhyayanaṃ duḥkhavighātāstrayaḥ suhṛtprāptiḥ dānaṃ ca siddhayo@ṣṭau siddheḥ pūrvo@ṅkuśastrividhaḥ

plain_english: Above the worlds beginning with aṇimā there are three rows connected with teacher and disciple. Their threefold division is explained by the influence of the three qualities.
sanskrit_cite: aṇimādyūrdhvatastisraḥ paṅktayo guruśiṣyagāḥ tatrāpi triguṇacchāyāyogāt tritvamudāhṛtam

plain_english: Above those rows is the eightfold set of nāḍī-knowledges beginning with iḍā. In the soul there is established a power made of sound, called expansion.
sanskrit_cite: nāḍīvidyāṣṭakaṃ cordhvaṃ paṅktīnāṃ syādiḍādikam puṃsi nādamayī śaktiḥ prasarākhyā ca yatsthitā

plain_english: A soul that is not an agent cannot truly be established as the doer. Even if the soul is not an agent, it may still stand as an assisting cause.
sanskrit_cite: na hyakartā pumānkartuḥ kāraṇatvaṃ ca saṃsthitam akartaryapi vā puṃsi sahakāritayā sthite

plain_english: Otherwise one would have to treat the soul as part of the effect, which would undermine the doctrine that the effect pre-exists. Therefore, in such a case, there is a specific power belonging to the soul.
sanskrit_cite: śeṣakāryātmataiṣṭavyānyathā satkāryahānitaḥ tasmāttathāvidhe kārye yā śaktiḥ puruṣasya sā

plain_english: Taking on that many forms, that power attains fullness. Above the eight nāḍīs, an eightfold set of forms is taught.
sanskrit_cite: tāvanti rūpāṇyādāya pūrṇatāmadhigacchati nāḍyaṣṭakordhve kathitaṃ vigrahāṣṭakamucyate

plain_english: At the level of the puruṣa principle there is an eightfold embodied set: effect, cause, suffering, pleasure, knowledge, what is to be accomplished, the instruments, and the means.
sanskrit_cite: kāryaṃ heturduḥkhaṃ sukhaṃ ca vijñānasādhyakaraṇāni sādhanamiti vigrahatāyugaṣṭakaṃ bhavati puṃstattve

plain_english: Beyond the eightfold forms is the world of the ten bodily observances: non-harm, truth, non-stealing, continence, freedom from deceit, freedom from anger, and duties toward the teacher.
sanskrit_cite: bhuvanaṃ dehadharmāṇāṃ daśānāṃ vigrahāṣṭakāt ahiṃsā satyamasteyaṃ brahmākalkākrudho guroḥ

plain_english: In the principle of the person are the ten declared qualities, including service, purity, contentment, and straightness. There too is situated a sixteenfold set ending with smell.
sanskrit_cite: śuśrūṣāśaucasantoṣā ṛjuteti daśoditāḥ puṃstattva eva gandhāntaṃ sthitaṃ ṣoḍaśakaṃ punaḥ

plain_english: Starting from the world called the body-bond, the qualities of intellect appear. There the ego is present in eightfold and threefold forms, along with bonds beginning with desire.
sanskrit_cite: ārabhya dehapāśākhyaṃ puraṃ buddhiguṇāstataḥ tatraivāṣṭāvahaṃkārastridhā kāmādikāstathā

plain_english: The bonds are threefold: adventitious, of the Ganeshas, and of the Vidyeshvaras. They are present in the person and block the path to liberation.
sanskrit_cite: pāśā āgantukagāṇeśavaidyeśvarabheditāḥ trividhāste sthitāḥ puṃsi mokṣamārgoparodhakāḥ

plain_english: Whatever is other than the supreme Shiva, whose nature is nondual consciousness, freedom, and beauty, is called a bond.
sanskrit_cite: yatkiṃcitparamādvaitasaṃvitsvātantryasundarāt parācchivāduktarūpādanyattatpāśa ucyate

plain_english: Thus, even though the supreme Lord remains full, when personhood is assumed there arises a wondrous non-recognition of his own nature; from that come persons.
sanskrit_cite: tadevaṃ puṃstvamāpanne pūrṇe@pi parameśvare tatsvarūpāparijñānaṃ citraṃ hi puruṣāstataḥ

plain_english: All the bonds, whether stated or unstated and described in the Paratantra, are present in the person. By purifying them there, one is freed from worldly becoming.
sanskrit_cite: uktānuktāstu ye pāśāḥ paratantroktalakṣaṇāḥ te puṃsi sarve tāṃstatra śodhayanmucyate bhavāt

plain_english: Above the person, in niyati, dwell ten Shankaras, golden and very white. In the principle of time dwell ten Shivas.
sanskrit_cite: puṃsa ūrdhva tu niyatistatrasthāḥ śaṃkarā daśa hemābhāḥ susitāḥ kālatattve tu daśa te śivāḥ

plain_english: In raga is the world of Viresha, a city of teachers and students, with ten million and sixteen thousand attendants for each.
sanskrit_cite: koṭiḥ ṣoḍaśasāhasraṃ pratyekaṃ parivāriṇaḥ rāge vīreśabhuvanaṃ gurvantevāsināṃ puram

plain_english: In impure knowledge there is a world shining with nine Shaktis, beginning with Vama and extending up to Manonmani.
sanskrit_cite: puraṃ cāśuddhavidyāyāṃ syācchaktinavakojjvalam manonmanyantagāstāśca vāmādyāḥ parikīrtitāḥ

plain_english: In kala is the supreme world of the three great gods. Beyond that is maya, a threefold domain filled chiefly with countless millions.
sanskrit_cite: kalāyāṃ syānmahādevatrayasya puramuttamam tato māyā tripuṭikā mukhyato@nantakoṭibhiḥ

plain_english: That maya is pervaded by cavities called bhaga, as taught in the Shaiva scripture. Again, there is a group of eight great gods extending to the measure of a thumb at night.
sanskrit_cite: ākrāntā sā bhagabilaiḥ proktaṃ śaivyāṃ tanau punaḥ aṅguṣṭhamātraparyantaṃ mahādevāṣṭakaṃ niśi

plain_english: Likewise, in the teaching of Shrimalini, the powers beginning with Vama are described as ruling the eight circles; in the earlier sacred teaching they are said to begin from the level of the person.
sanskrit_cite: cakrāṣṭakādhipatyena tathā śrīmālinīmate vāmādyāḥ puruṣādau ye proktāḥ śrīpūrvaśāsane

plain_english: In the Shaiva scripture they are placed in the principle of maya, under Ananta: skull-vow observers, those who offer their own limbs, and practitioners of harsh austerities.
sanskrit_cite: te māyātattva evoktāstanau śaivyāmanantataḥ kapālavratinaḥ svāṅgahotāraḥ kaṣṭatāpasāḥ

plain_english: Fearless and observing the sword-edge vow, knowing the principles, they gradually ascend through each principle until they reach the place where the lord is called Ananta.
sanskrit_cite: sarvābhayāḥ khaḍgadhārāvratāstattattvavedinaḥ kramāttattattvamāyānti yatreśo@nanta ucyate

plain_english: And it is said that beyond him is the abode of the lord of Ananta, the god who performs creation, maintenance, and dissolution, and who guards the door of the cave and the bhaga.
sanskrit_cite: uktaṃ ca tasya parataḥ sthānamanantādhipasya devasya sthitivilayasargakarturguhābhagadvārapālasya

plain_english: Drawing them out again and again from the cavity of maya, he bestows on persons merits, powers such as minuteness, knowledges, austerities, pleasures, and yogic attainments.
sanskrit_cite: dharmānaṇimādiguṇāñjñānāni tapaḥsukhāni yogāṃśca māyābilātpradatte puṃsāṃ niṣkṛṣya niṣkṛṣya

plain_english: Empowered by his energy, all the lords from Ananta onward, down to those beginning with Shatabhava, shine like lamps dispelling darkness in the office of the cave.
sanskrit_cite: tacchaktīddhasvabalā guhādhikārāndhakāraguṇadīpāḥ sarve@nantapramukhā dīpyante śatabhavapramukhāntāḥ

plain_english: Presiding over the unmanifest, Shiva brings forth the world by the command of Shambhu, because he is the cause of authority over both the pure and impure streams.
sanskrit_cite: so@vyaktamadhiṣṭhāya prakaroti jaganniyogataḥ śambhoḥ śuddhāśuddhasroto@dhikārahetuḥ śivo yasmāt

plain_english: Those first established in that great station endowed with Shiva's qualities, beginning with Ananta, become the agents of the world's creation, maintenance, and dissolution.
sanskrit_cite: śivaguṇayoge tasmin mahati pade ye pratiṣṭhitāḥ prathamam te@nantāderjagataḥ sargasthitivilayakartāraḥ

plain_english: This has been called the cavity of maya. Beyond it is the cave, the womb of the world, where generation occurs as the stirring of the lord's power takes effect.
sanskrit_cite: māyābilamidamuktaṃ paratastu guhā jagadyoniḥ utpattyā teṣvasyāḥ patiśaktikṣobhamanuvidhīyamāneṣu

plain_english: In the womb-openings, rich with various desires and called bhaga, when the lord desires the goddess who follows his will, the generative process begins.
sanskrit_cite: yonivivareṣu nānākāmasamṛddheṣu bhagasaṃjñā kāmayate patirenāmicchānuvidhāyinīṃ yadā devīm

plain_english: In each bhaga, offspring beginning with the unmanifest are born from her. They are so extremely subtle that their nature is not described in the prescribed texts.
sanskrit_cite: pratibhagamavyaktādyāḥ prajāstadāsyāḥ prajāyante teṣāmatisūkṣmāṇāmetāvattvaṃ na varṇyate vidhiṣu

plain_english: Just as many enclosed inner rooms can exist within one hall, so many womb-cavities exist within the single head-hall of maya.
sanskrit_cite: avavarakāṇyekasminyadvatsāle bahūni baddhāni yonibilānyekasmiṃstadvanmāyāśiraḥsāle

plain_english: Covered by subtle layers and walls of maya, invisible to one another, countless happy Rudras dwell there in each cavity.
sanskrit_cite: māyāpaṭalaiḥ sūkṣmaiḥ kuḍyaiḥ pihitāḥ parasparamadṛśyāḥ nivasanti tatra rudrāḥ sukhinaḥ pratibilamasaṃkhyātāḥ

plain_english: Dwellers in each world are taught by teachers as having attained union, proximity, or supreme same-world residence.
sanskrit_cite: sthāne sāyujyagatāḥ sāmīpyagatāḥ pare salokasthāḥ pratibhuvanamevamayaṃ nivāsināṃ gurubhiruddiṣṭaḥ

plain_english: Even words of the accomplished, uttered long ago, are worn out; numbers of streams are not spoken again from endless rebirth.
sanskrit_cite: api sarvasiddhavācaḥ kṣīyerandīrghakālamudgīrṇāḥ na punaryonyānantyāducyante srotasāṃ saṃkhyāḥ

plain_english: Therefore, from one hell up to door guardians, other streams too are similarly arranged and to be known.
sanskrit_cite: tasmānnirayādyekaṃ yatproktaṃ dvārapālaparyantam srotastenānyānyapi tulyavidhānāni vedyāni

plain_english: In unmanifest time, by cave, nature, and art, the own modification is woven across and through, pervaded, measured, full, and encircled.
sanskrit_cite: avyaktakale guhayā prakṛtikalābhyāṃ vikāra ātmīyaḥ otaḥ proto vyāptaḥ kalitaḥ pūrṇaḥ parikṣiptaḥ

plain_english: In the middle, three sheaths of that contain rudras: six in the lower interval, one above, and five; these twelve are determined.
sanskrit_cite: madhye puṭatrayaṃ tasyā rudrāḥ ṣaḍadhare@ntare eka ūrdhve ca pañceti dvādaśaite nirūpitāḥ

plain_english: The deep difficult lords, hari, hara, dasha lords, and three-time lords; these six in the endless middle are auspicious brahman-lord, knowledge-lord, world-shiva.
sanskrit_cite: gahanāsādhyau hariharadaśeśvarau trikalagopatī ṣaḍime madhye@nantaḥ kṣemo dvijeśavidyeśaviśvaśivāḥ

plain_english: Thus in those five and six sheaths, by turning of that, position revolves; indeed the endless god is in every way in the middle.
sanskrit_cite: iti pañca teṣu pañcasu ṣaṭsu ca puṭageṣu tatparāvṛttyā parivarttate sthitiḥ kila devo@nantastu sarvathā madhye

plain_english: By the pair of six upper and lower skull sheaths, by turning of that, pervaded in the middle by eight directional ones, the knot stated in Matanga scripture.
sanskrit_cite: ūrdhvādharagakapālakapuṭaṣaṭkayugena tatparāvṛttyā madhyato@ṣṭābhirdiksthairvyāpto granthirmataṅgaśāstroktaḥ

plain_english: In the Sri Sara teaching, again this is declared as six sheaths; this knot-principle is the work of maya, then maya.
