sanskrit_cite: śrīsāraśāsane punareṣā ṣaṭpuṭatayā vinirdiṣṭā granthyākhyamidaṃ tattvaṃ māyākāryaṃ tato māyā

plain_english: The maya principle is indeed pervasive, deep, formless, place of all dissolution; there world-division is not fit, that knot therefore.
sanskrit_cite: māyātattvaṃ vibhu kila gahanamarūpaṃ samastavilayapadam tatra na bhuvanavibhāgo yukto granthāvasau tasmāt

plain_english: The endless lord of maya principle simultaneously agitates collected atoms; she produces night by endless own enclosures.
sanskrit_cite: māyātattvādhipatiḥ so@nantaḥ samuditānvicāryāṇūn yugapatkṣobhayati niśāṃ sā sūte saṃpuṭairanantaiḥ svaiḥ

plain_english: By that, the declared veil net from kala to earth end is countless and various; maya alone is one and to be distinguished.
sanskrit_cite: tena kalādidharāntaṃ yaduktamāvaraṇajālamakhilaṃ tat niḥsaṃkhyaṃ ca vicitraṃ māyaivaikā tvabhinneyam

plain_english: It is said in the Sri prior scripture: the earth-manifest pair is countless, called night-power, but one-natured.
sanskrit_cite: uktaṃ śrīpūrvaśāstre ca dharāvyaktātmakaṃ dvayam asaṃkhyātaṃ niśāśaktisaṃjñaṃ tvekasvarūpakam

plain_english: Bonds previously said, om-syllables, five-eight, sage's family and womb, speech-goddess; one born in her is not born again.
sanskrit_cite: pāśāḥ puroktāḥ praṇavāḥ pañcamānāṣṭakaṃ muneḥ kulaṃ yoniśca vāgīśī yasyāṃ jāto na jāyate

plain_english: At initiation time, in earth-path purification, all that goes the earth path of the endless is fully established near him.
sanskrit_cite: dīkṣākāle@dharādhvasthaśuddhau yaccādharādhvagam anantasya samīpe tu tatsarvaṃ pariniṣṭhitam

plain_english: Accomplishable, giver, subduer, meditator, ash: five dots, with formation, marked by five-meaning secret rudra goad heart.
sanskrit_cite: sādhyo dātā damano dhyāno bhasmeti bindavaḥ pañca pañcārthaguhyarudrāṅkuśahṛdayalakṣaṇaṃ ca savyūham

plain_english: Attraction and mirror, this eight of measures; all with unlost powers are authorities of maya principle.
sanskrit_cite: ākarṣādarśau cetyaṣṭakametatpramāṇānām aluptavibhavāḥ sarve māyātattvādhikāriṇaḥ

plain_english: Those with maya bodies enjoy their own enjoyment; at the end of dissolution, indeed by the endless, they are withdrawn, but at day's beginning.
sanskrit_cite: māyāmayaśarīrāste bhogaṃ svaṃ paribhuñjate pralayānte hyanantena saṃhṛtāste tvaharmukhe

plain_english: By the grace of another endless, even wise ones think the supreme asleep-awakened, dull with self-will opinion.
sanskrit_cite: anyānantaprasādena vibudhā api taṃ param suptabuddhaṃ manyamānāḥ svatantrammanyatājaḍāḥ

plain_english: Those situated in the maya interval know only their own self as cause; therefore maya goddess stands supreme, deluding creatures.
sanskrit_cite: svātmānameva jānanti hetuṃ māyāntarālagāḥ ataḥ paraṃ sthitā māyā devī jantuvimohinī

plain_english: She is the power of the god of gods, doing very difficult things, obstructing without enmity; by her minds are made to wander.
sanskrit_cite: devadevasya sā śaktiratidurghaṭakāritā nirvairaparipanthinyā tayā bhramitabuddhayaḥ

plain_english: Disputants here dispute this principle, this not-this; those not devoted to guru, deva, agni scriptures are lowest men.
sanskrit_cite: idaṃ tattvamidaṃ neti vivadantīha vādinaḥ gurudevāgniśāstreṣu ye na bhaktā narādhamāḥ

plain_english: Abandoning the true path, it certainly leads them to the false path, those clinging to dry logic.
sanskrit_cite: satpathaṃ tānparityājya sotpathaṃ nayati dhruvam asadyuktivicārajñāñchuṣkatarkāvalambinaḥ

plain_english: Maya indeed deludes them in non-liberation, with desire for liberation; thus cut by the sword of shiva initiation and the sword of shiva knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: bhramayatyeva tānmāyā hyamokṣe mokṣalipsayā śivadīkṣāsinā cchinnā śivajñānāsinā tathā

plain_english: No other cause sprouts again; cutting is directed toward it, and pure great knowledge stands above great maya.
sanskrit_cite: na prarohetpunarnānyo hetustacchedanaṃ prati mahāmāyordhvataḥ śuddhā mahāvidyātha mātṛkā

plain_english: Vageshvari stands there in the city of nine, including Vama, Jyeshtha, Raudri, Kali, Kalavikarani, Balavikarika, and others.
sanskrit_cite: vāgīśvarī ca tatrasthaṃ vāmādinavasatpuram vāmā jyeṣṭhā raudrī kālī kalavikaraṇībalavikārike tathā

plain_english: Mathani, Damani, Manonmani, and all those yellow powers amount to seven crores of chief mantra powers established in the knowledge principle.
sanskrit_cite: mathanī damanī manonmanī ca tridṛśaḥ pītāḥ samastāstāḥ saptakoṭyo mukhyamantrā vidyātattve@tra saṃsthitāḥ

plain_english: Here there are lotus-shaped cities, seven knowledge queens beginning with triguna, and seven arbuda lords.
sanskrit_cite: ekaikārbudalakṣāṃśāḥ padmākārapurā iha vidyārājñyastriguṇyādyāḥ sapta saptārbudeśvarāḥ

plain_english: Above the knowledge principle is the aisha principle, ascending in order from Shikhanda to Ananta, joined with eight cities.
sanskrit_cite: vidyātattvordhvamaiśaṃ tu tattvaṃ tatra kramordhvagam śikhaṇḍyādyamanantāntaṃ purāṣṭakayutaṃ puram

plain_english: Shikhanda, Shrigala, Murti, one-eye, one-rudra, highest Shiva, subtle Rudra, Ananta, and the eight Vidyeshvaras are named.
sanskrit_cite: śikhaṇḍī śrīgalo mūrtirekanetraikarudrakau śivottamaḥ sūkṣmarudro@nanto vidyeśvarāṣṭakam

plain_english: In the ascending upward placement of the seven, Ananta is the leader and lord, to be meditated and worshipped increasingly.
sanskrit_cite: kramādūrdhvordhvasaṃsthānaṃ saptānāṃ nāyako vibhuḥ ananta eva dhyeyaśca pūjyaścāpyuttarottaraḥ

plain_english: Three crores are established with the chief mantra lords; these leaders are thereby Vidyeshas and world rulers.
sanskrit_cite: mukhyamantreśvarāṇāṃ yat sārdhaṃ koṭitrayaṃ sthitam tannāyakā ime tena vidyeśāścakravartinaḥ

plain_english: The gurus said this in the Shiva-body teachings: a god with eight shakti pairs sits on the guha throne.
sanskrit_cite: uktaṃ ca gurubhiritthaṃ śivatanvādyeṣu śāsaneṣvetat bhagabilaśatakalitaguhāmūrdhāsanago@ṣṭaśaktiyugdevaḥ

plain_english: From the deep beginning to the end of hell, he creates, assigns Rudras, and uplifts men through Manonmani, remaining middle-standing.
sanskrit_cite: gahanādyaṃ nirayāntaṃ sṛjati ca rudrāṃśca viniyuṅkte uddharati manonmanyā puṃsasteṣveva bhavati madhyasthaḥ

plain_english: Those uplifted by him enter supreme principle contemplation; he is again appointed by Shiva among path dwellers and atoms.
sanskrit_cite: te tenodastacitaḥ paratattvālocane@bhiniviśante sa punaradhaḥ pathavartiṣvadhikṛta evāṇuṣu śivena

plain_english: After the completed lord assignment, Ananta lord enters that abode with many soul mantra crores, while subtle Rudra extinguishes.
sanskrit_cite: avasitapativiniyogaḥ sārdhamanekātmamantrakoṭībhiḥ nirvātyanantanāthastaddhāmāviśati sūkṣmarudrastu

plain_english: The lord establishes the first atom in Shikhanda's place; thus eight proceed in order until the abodes, by the single guru.
sanskrit_cite: anugṛhyāṇumapūrvaṃ sthāpayati patiḥ śikhaṇḍinaḥ sthāne ityaṣṭau paripāṭyā yāvaddhāmāni yāti gururekaḥ

plain_english: Those eight, seated on lotus thrones with eight shakti yoga, make liberation for countless beings.
sanskrit_cite: tāvadasaṃkhyātānāṃ jantūnāṃ nirvṛtiṃ kurute te@ṣṭāvapi śaktyaṣṭakayogāmalajalaruhāsanāsīnāḥ

plain_english: They behold the god dwelling in the heart, the supreme cause Ananta, meditating on the peaceful cause in their own heart.
sanskrit_cite: ālokayanti devaṃ hṛdayasthaṃ kāraṇaṃ paramam taṃ bhagavantamanantaṃ dhyāyantaḥ svahṛdi kāraṇaṃ śāntam

plain_english: Seven crores of pure mantras meditate, extending from Maya to sun ray; becoming is called non-becoming beginning with Ananta.
sanskrit_cite: saptānudhyāyantyapi mantrāṇāṃ koṭayaḥ śuddhāḥ māyādiravīcyanto bhavastvanantādirucyate@pyabhavaḥ

plain_english: This end of Shiva pure quality authority is also rejected here, because the appointability of the seen and granted is Shaiva.
sanskrit_cite: śivaśuddhaguṇādhīkārāntaḥ so@pyeṣa heyaśca atrāpi yato dṛṣṭānugrāhyāṇāṃ niyojyatā śaivī

plain_english: Desired cessation is non-becoming below, but it does not become so, because it departs from the lord; causality and effecthood come from the accomplished.
sanskrit_cite: iṣṭā ca tannivṛttirhyabhavastvadhare na bhūyate yasmāt patyurapasarpati yataḥ kāraṇatā kāryatā ca siddhebhyaḥ

plain_english: In Shiva accomplishment like armor, the extreme and middle-standing pair is named, and the city of four—dharma, knowledge, dispassion, and mastery—is identified.
sanskrit_cite: kañcukavacchivasiddhau tāvatibhavasaṃjñayātimadhyasthau dharmajñānavirāgaiśyacatuṣṭayapuraṃ tu yat

plain_english: In this Ishvara principle, the form covering is known; Vama, Jyeshtha, and Raudri adorn the three worlds.
sanskrit_cite: rūpāvaraṇasaṃjñaṃ tattattve@sminnaiśvare viduḥ vāmā jyeṣṭhā ca raudrīti bhuvanatrayaśobhitam

plain_english: The subtle covering in the Isha principle, named by the best gurus, runs from Aisha to Sadashiva and is adorned with the knowledge-action pair.
sanskrit_cite: sūkṣmāvaraṇamākhyātamīśatattve gurūttamaiḥ aiśātsādāśivaṃ jñānakriyāyugalamaṇḍitam

plain_english: The pure covering is thus said; from it comes the supreme, and then the knowledge covering shines with two powers of being and non-being.
sanskrit_cite: śuddhāvaraṇamityāhuruktā śuddhāvṛteḥ param vidyāvṛtistato bhāvābhāvaśaktidvayojjvalā

plain_english: The power covering, called measure, is determined in scripture; it is adorned by Tejasvi and Dhruvesha.
sanskrit_cite: śaktyāvṛtiḥ pramāṇākhyā tataḥ śāstre nirūpitā śaktyāvṛtestu tejasvidhruveśābhyāmalaṅkṛtam

plain_english: The Tejasvi covering is followed by the measure covering, which is adorned with three pure covering cities.
sanskrit_cite: tejasvyāvaraṇaṃ vedapurā mānāvṛtistataḥ mānāvṛteḥ suśuddhāvṛtpuratritayaśobhitā

plain_english: Above the very-pure covering there is a single Shaiva city. Above the Shiva-covering, they say, lies the covering called the liberation-covering.
sanskrit_cite: suśuddhāvaraṇādūrdhva śaivamekapuraṃ bhavet śivāvṛterūrdhvamāhurmokṣāvaraṇasaṃjñitam

plain_english: In this liberation-covering, eleven Rudras are described. Above the liberation-covering there is a single-city covering called the fixed one.
sanskrit_cite: asyāṃ mokṣāvṛtau rudrā ekādaśa nirūpitāḥ mokṣāvaraṇatastvekapuramāvaraṇaṃ dhruvam

plain_english: Above the fixed covering is the will-covering. There dwell those Shivas inside the house of the Lord's will, and that city is said to be one.
sanskrit_cite: ūrdhve dhruvāvṛtericchāvaraṇaṃ tatra te śivāḥ īśvarecchāgṛhāntasthāstatpuraṃ caikamucyate

plain_english: Above the will-covering is the one called the awakened covering, frequented by the eight directional Rudras. Above the awakened covering lies the great covenant-covering.
sanskrit_cite: icchāvṛteḥ prabuddhākhyaṃ digrudrāṣṭakacarcitam prabuddhāvaraṇādūrdhva samayāvaraṇaṃ mahat

plain_english: The covenant-covering encloses the covering of Ananta within five worlds. Above it lies the auspicious-Shiva realm, and there is the great world called Sadakhya.
sanskrit_cite: bhuvanaiḥ pañcabhirgarbhīkṛtānantasamāvṛti sāmayātsauśivaṃ tatra sādākhyaṃ bhuvanaṃ mahat

plain_english: In that world dwells the god Sadashiva. His powers of knowledge and action are on his left and right, while his supreme will rests in his lap.
sanskrit_cite: tasminsadāśivo devastasya savyāpasavyayoḥ jñānakriye parecchā tu śaktirutsaṅgagāminī

plain_english: By that will, Sadashiva performs the five acts beginning with creation. With him are the five Brahmas, the six limbs, the group of eight beginning with Sakala, and other Shivas.
sanskrit_cite: sṛṣṭyādipañcakṛtyāni kurute sa tayecchayā pañca brahmāṇyaṅgaṣaṭkaṃ sakalādyaṣṭakaṃ śivāḥ

plain_english: The auspicious Shiva is surrounded by those ten and eighteen Rudras. The five Brahmas are Sadyojata, Vama, Aghora, Purusha, and Ishana, and the heart is named among them.
sanskrit_cite: daśāṣṭādaśa rudrāśca taireva suśivo vṛtaḥ sadyo vāmāghorau puruṣeśau brahmapañcakaṃ hṛdayam

plain_english: They declare the six limbs to be head, tuft, armor, eye, and weapon, together with the heart. Along with them are Sakala, Akala, Shunya, Kaladhya, Kha, and Kshapana as the last.
sanskrit_cite: mūrdhaśikhāvarmadṛgastramaṅgāni ṣaṭ prāhuḥ sakalākalaśūnyaiḥ saha kalāḍhyakhamalaṅkṛte kṣapaṇamantyam

plain_english: The throat-and-lip one is the eighth, and this group of eight Saktalas is traditionally transmitted. Then are named Omkara, Shiva, Dipta, Hetu, Isha, Dasheshaka, Sushiva, and Kala.
sanskrit_cite: kaṇṭhyauṣṭhyamaṣṭamaṃ kila sakalāṣṭakametadāmnātam oṃ kāraśivau dīpto hetvīśadaśeśakau suśivakālau

plain_english: Sukshma, Sutejas, and Sharva are these ten Shivas. Then, beginning from the east, come Vijaya, Nihshvasa, Svayambhuva, Vahni, Vira, and Raurava.
sanskrit_cite: sūkṣmasutejaḥśarvāḥ śivāḥ daśaite@tra pūrvādeḥ vijayo niḥśvāsaśca svāyambhuvo vahnivīrarauravakāḥ

plain_english: Mukuta, Visara, Indu, Bindu, Prodgita, Lalita, Siddha, Rudra, Santana, Shiva, Para, Kirana, and Paramesha are remembered as the Rudras.
sanskrit_cite: mukuṭavisarenduvinduprodgītā lalitasiddharudrau ca santānaśivau parakiraṇapārameśā iti smṛtā rudrāḥ

plain_english: All these Rudras have knowledges that bear names equal to their own. They are surrounded by crores of mantra-sages and joined with Vibhu, Vama, and the Rudras together with their powers.
sanskrit_cite: sarveṣāmeteṣāṃ jñānāni viduḥ svatulyanāmāni mantramunikoṭiparivṛta matha vibhuvāmādirudratacchaktiyutam

plain_english: Sushiva's seat is a very white lotus with countless petals, endowed with Tara and other powers. The group of powers and Rudras is present both in his retinue and on his seat.
sanskrit_cite: tārādiśaktijuṣṭaṃ suśivāsanamatisitakajamasaṃkhyadalam yaḥ śaktirudravargaḥ parivāre viṣṭare ca suśivasya

plain_english: In each one's own retinue there are countless crores beyond measure. They are freed from the impurity of maya, yet remain established only in their office.
sanskrit_cite: pratyekamasya nijanijaparivāre parārdhakoṭayo@saṃkhyāḥ māyāmalanirmuktāḥ kevalamadhikāramātrasaṃrūḍhāḥ

plain_english: In the covering of Sushiva, the Rudras are all-knowing and full of all powers. When the bondage of their office dissolves, they become peaceful, take on the form of Shiva, and are no longer subject to rebirth.
sanskrit_cite: suśivāvaraṇe rudrāḥ sarvajñāḥ sarvaśaktisampūrṇāḥ adhikārabandhavilaye śāntāḥ śivarūpiṇo punarbhavinaḥ

plain_english: Above is the radiant covering of bindu. There is a moon-bright lotus, and there Shiva as Shantyatita is adorned, resting in the lap of his power.
sanskrit_cite: ūrdhve bindvāvṛtirdīptā tatra tatra padmaṃ śaśiprabham śāntyatītaḥ śivastatra tacchaktyutsaṅgabhūṣitaḥ

plain_english: He is surrounded by the retinue of the kala group beginning with Nivritti, and by crores of cities of countless Rudras and their powers.
sanskrit_cite: nivṛttyādikalāvargaparivārasamāvṛtaḥ asaṃkhyarudratacchaktipurakoṭibhirāvṛtaḥ

plain_english: In the revered Matanga scripture, the highest principle called Laya is, by that technical name, identified here with bindu.
sanskrit_cite: śrīmanmataṅgaśāstre ca layākhyaṃ tattvamuttamam pāribhāṣikamityetannāmnā bindurihocyate

plain_english: That bright principle, made of four forms and both with parts and without parts, is where enjoyment is said to take place. This is how it is described here.
sanskrit_cite: caturmūrtimayaṃ śubhraṃ yattatsakalaniṣkalam tasminbhogaḥ samuddiṣṭa ityatredaṃ ca varṇitam

plain_english: Because Nivritti and the other kalas are extremely subtle, embodiment beginning from earth does not take shape in the usual way. Since the Mother is absorbed in flashing great knowledge, it is not distinctly perceived.
sanskrit_cite: nivṛttyādeḥ susūkṣmatvāddharādyārabdhadehatā mātuḥ sphūrjanmahājñānalīnatvānna vibhāvyate

plain_english: Just as earth particles in gold do not appear separately because its fiery nature predominates, so too the elements in the bodies of the higher and lower Rudras do not appear separately.
sanskrit_cite: udrikta taijasatvena hemno bhūparamāṇavaḥ yathā pṛthaṅna bhāntyevamūrdhvādhorudradehagāḥ

plain_english: Above bindu is the half-moon. From that come kala, moonlight, radiance, splendor, and the pure one. These five are the obstructing powers.
sanskrit_cite: bindūrdhve@rdhenduretasya kalā jyotsnā ca tadvatī kāntiḥ prabhā ca vimalā pañcaitā rodhikāstataḥ

plain_english: The best of teachers declare that in Nirodhini there are five kalas: Rundhani, Rodhani, Roddhri, Jnanabodha, and Tamopaha.
sanskrit_cite: rundhanī rodhanī roddhrī jñānabodhā tamopahā etāḥ pañca kalāḥ prāhurnirodhinyāṃ gurūttamāh

plain_english: The half-measure is called bindu, which has the form of space and four phases. Half of that is the half-moon, and by an eighth part of that comes nirodhikā.
sanskrit_cite: ardhamātraḥ smṛto bindurvyomarūpī catuṣkalaḥ tadardhamardhacandrastadaṣṭāṃśena nirodhikā

plain_english: Rodhikā blocks the causal lords beginning with Brahma; one should abandon it. Then, after piercing this nirodhikā, one reaches the supreme world called Sadakhya.
sanskrit_cite: hetūnbrahmādikān runddhe rodhikāṃ tāṃ tyajettataḥ nirodhikāmimāṃ bhittvā sādākhyaṃ bhuvanaṃ param

plain_english: There, in supreme form, abides the one whose great body is made of the five mantras. Thus, above the covering of bindu that ends in the half-moon and nirodhi, there is a great presence.
sanskrit_cite: pararūpeṇa yatrāste pañcamantramahātanuḥ ityardhendunirodhyantabindvāvṛtyūrdhvato mahān

plain_english: Nāda is like the filaments of a flower and is surrounded by great beings. There are four worlds in the directions and a fifth in the center.
sanskrit_cite: nādaḥ kiñjalkasadṛśo mahadbhiḥ puruṣairvṛtaḥ catvāri bhuvanānyatra dikṣu madhye ca pañcamam

plain_english: Indhikā, Dīpikā, Rodhikā, and the upward-going Mocikā are there. In the middle is a lotus, and there the upward-moving one is surrounded by its powers.
sanskrit_cite: indhikā dīpikā caiva rodhikā mocikordhvagā madhye@tra padmaṃ tatrordhvagāmī tacchaktibhirvṛtaḥ

plain_english: Above nāda is the suṣumna realm. There the lord who bears its powers is surrounded on the left and right by Piṅgalā and Iḍā.
sanskrit_cite: nādordhvatastu sauṣumnaṃ tatra tacchaktibhṛtprabhuḥ tadīśaḥ piṅgalelābhyāṃ vṛtaḥ savyāpasavyayoḥ

plain_english: The goddess Suṣumnā, resting in the lord's lap and shining like the moon, strings together the whole path, both above and below.
sanskrit_cite: yā prabhoraṅkagā devī suṣumnā śaśisaprabhā grathito@dhvā tayā sarva ūrdhvaścādhastanastathā

plain_english: The support of nāda and suṣumnā pierces this entire universe; it goes out below by the downward power and above from the crown by the upward power.
sanskrit_cite: nādaḥsuṣumnādhārastu bhittvā viśvamidaṃ jagat adhaḥśaktyā vinirgacchedūrdhvaśaktyā ca mūrdhataḥ

plain_english: Absorbed through the channel in the cavity of Brahma, that unmanifest, resonant, imperishable sound resounds in all beings, empowered by Śiva's śakti.
sanskrit_cite: nāḍyā brahmabile līnaḥ so@vyaktadhvanirakṣaraḥ nadansarveṣu bhūteṣu śivaśaktyā hyadhiṣṭhitaḥ

plain_english: Above Suṣumnā is the covering called the brahma cavity. There dwells Brahmā, white, three-eyed, bearing a trident, five-faced, and crowned with the moon.
sanskrit_cite: suṣumnordhve brahmabilasaṃjñayāvaraṇaṃ tridṛk tatra brahmā sitaḥ śūlī pañcāsyaḥ śaśiśekharaḥ

plain_english: In his lap sits the supreme goddess Brahmāṇī, who moves on the path of liberation and both obstructs and grants release. Piercing through her, one comes to the upward Kuṇḍalinī.
sanskrit_cite: tasyotsaṅge parā devī brahmāṇī mokṣamārgagā roddhrī dātrī ca mokṣasya tāṃ bhittvā cordhvakuṇḍalī

plain_english: That śakti is like a sleeping serpent and is called the support of the universe. Within her are the subtle, the very subtle, Amṛtā, Amitā, and other powers.
sanskrit_cite: śaktiḥ suptāhisadṛśī sā viśvādhāra ucyate tasyāṃ sūkṣmā susūkṣmā ca tathānye amṛtāmite

plain_english: In the middle is Vyāpinī, and within her is Vyāpīśa, the bearer of Vyāpinī. This is the śakti principle, whose manifestation extends all the way down to earth.
sanskrit_cite: madhyato vyāpinī tasyāṃ vyāpīśo vyāpinīdharaḥ śaktitattvamidaṃ yasya prapañco@yaṃ dharāntakaḥ

plain_english: Then comes the Śiva principle. Established in the four directions are Vyāpī, the sky-natured lord Ananta, and those who share in his powers.
sanskrit_cite: śivatattvaṃ tatastatra caturdikkaṃ vyavasthitāḥ vyāpī vyomātmako@nanto@nāthastacchaktibhāginaḥ

plain_english: In the middle there is the unsupported one: the god of gods, Anāśrita, bearing his śakti in his lap and shining with the radiance of a hundred crore suns.
sanskrit_cite: madhye tvanāśritaṃ tatra devadevo hyanāśritaḥ tacchaktyutsaṅgabhṛtsūryaśatakoṭisamaprabhaḥ

plain_english: Above the Śiva principle is the supreme śakti called Samanā. She abides as the active agent of all causes.
sanskrit_cite: śivatattvordhvataḥ śaktiḥ parā sā samanāhvayā sarveṣāṃ kāraṇānāṃ sā kartṛbhūtā vyavasthitā

plain_english: Empowered by Śiva, she bears many cosmic eggs. Resting upon her, Lord Śiva performs the five acts.
sanskrit_cite: bibhartyaṇḍānyanekāni śivena samadhiṣṭhitā tadārūḍhaḥ śivaḥ kṛtyapañcakaṃ kurute prabhuḥ

plain_english: Samanā is the instrument of that great causal lord. The unsupported principle, in activity, is the occasioning cause and is called the cause.
sanskrit_cite: samanā karaṇaṃ tasya hetukarturmahośituḥ anāśritaṃ tu vyāpāre nimittaṃ heturucyate

plain_english: Through her the all-pervading lord presides over the five causes. This unsupported, lordly, endless, sky-bodied one does so always.
sanskrit_cite: tayādhitiṣṭhati vibhuḥ kāraṇānāṃ tu pañcakam anāśrito@nāthamayamanantaṃ khavapuḥ sadā

plain_english: He impels the pervading lord by his own śakti as instrument. Below that abides Māyā in the form of karma, and below that is the śakti Kuṇḍalinī.
sanskrit_cite: sa vyāpinaṃ prerayati svaśaktyā karaṇena tu karmarūpā sthitā māyā yadadhaḥ śaktikuṇḍalī

plain_english: The arising of the world as effect begins with nāda, bindu, and so on. In the teaching, this includes everything from the earthly level up to Sadāśiva.
sanskrit_cite: nādabindvādikaṃ kāryamityādijagadudbhavaḥ yatsadāśivaparyantaṃ pārthivādyaṃ ca śāsane

plain_english: All that is declared to be produced and subject to arising and destruction. Now I will present the measure of all the worlds as it was taught to me by my own gurus.
sanskrit_cite: tatsarva prākṛtaṃ proktaṃ vināśotpattisaṃyutam atha sakalabhuvanamānaṃ yanmahyaṃ nigaditaṃ nijairgurubhiḥ

plain_english: That will now be explained briefly so that the mind may quickly move through it. Within the cosmic egg are Ananta, Kāla, Kūṣmāṇḍa and Hāṭaka, and Brahmā and Hari.
sanskrit_cite: tadvakṣyate samāsādbuddhau yenāśu saṅkrāmet aṇḍasyāntaranantaḥ kālaḥ kūṣmāṇḍahāṭakau brahmaharī

plain_english: There are one hundred Rudras with their hosts. Outside is Nivṛtti, which has one hundred and eight worlds, distributed individually across the sevenfold group of water, fire, wind, space, ego, intellect, and root.
sanskrit_cite: rudrāḥ śataṃ savīraṃ bahirnivṛttistu sāṣṭaśatabhuvanā syāt jalatejaḥsamīranabho@haṃkṛddhīmūlasaptake pratyekam

plain_english: The kalā level is declared to have fifty-six worlds, and so it is called pratiṣṭhā. Some, however, say that eight of its own lords are to be purified there.
sanskrit_cite: aṣṭau ṣaṭpañcāśadbhuvanā tena pratiṣṭheti kalā kathitā atra prāhuḥ śodhyānaṣṭau kecinnijāṣṭakādhipatīn

plain_english: Others say that all the worlds are to be purified. The teachers led by Śrī Bhūtirāja Miśra, however, say that a hundred Rudras are outside.
sanskrit_cite: anye tu samastānāṃ śodhyatvaṃ varṇayanti bhuvanānām śrībhūtirājamiśrā guravaḥ prāhuḥ punarbahī rudraśatam

plain_english: This nivṛtti consists of eight Rudras within, together with Śarva. The Rudras named here are Kālī, Vīra, Dharā, Abdhi, Lakṣmī, Sarasvatī, and Guhya.
sanskrit_cite: aṣṭāvantaḥ sākaṃ śarveṇetīdṛśī nivṛttiriyaṃ syāt rudrāḥ kālī vīro dharābdhilakṣmyaḥ sarasvatī guhyam

plain_english: Thus the group of eight is in water. In fire there is a pair beyond Guhya; in wind there is the world of Vāyu. In space there are the group beginning with Gaya, Vyoma, the eight Pavitras, and a pair of worlds.
sanskrit_cite: ityaṣṭakaṃ jale@nau vahnyatiguhyadvayaṃ maruti vāyoḥ svapuraṃ gayādi khe ca vyoma pavitrāṣṭakaṃ ca bhuvanayugam

plain_english: In ego there is the group of eight beginning with Chagala. Then, within the domain of space and ego-maker, there is the group of eight worlds of the tanmātras, sun, moon, and śruti, belonging to the gods of intellect and action.
sanskrit_cite: abhimāne@haṅkāracchagalādyaṣṭakamathāntarā nabho@haṃkṛt tanmātrārkenduśratipurāṣṭakaṃ buddhikarmadevānām

plain_english: There are ten worlds in the tanmātra group, and others in the sense group and in mind and ego; altogether there are twenty-two worlds.
sanskrit_cite: daśa tanmātrasamūhe bhuvanaṃ punarakṣavargavinipatite manasaścetyabhimāne dvāviṃśatireva bhuvanānām

plain_english: In the intellect there are eight divine ones, a triad called Kṛt, Tejas, and Yoga, then Umā and her lord, then the eight Mūrtis, the twelve Suśivas, and Vīrabhadra.
sanskrit_cite: dhiyi daivīnāmaṣṭau kruttejoyogasaṃjñakaṃ trayaṃ tadumā tatpatiratha mūrtyaṣṭakasuśivadvādaśakavīrabhadrāḥ syuḥ

plain_english: Then come the eight Mahādevas; in the intellect the count is seventeen. In the guṇa tattva there are three sets of five, and altogether they know fifty-six worlds.
sanskrit_cite: tadatha mahādevāṣṭakamiti buddhau saptadaśa saṃkhyā guṇatattve paṅktitrayamiti ṣaṭpañcāśataṃ purāṇi viduḥ

plain_english: Although the eight Krodheśvaras are in mūla, the state of balanced guṇas, they are not counted again in pratiṣṭhā because they are treated as purified in the intellect.
sanskrit_cite: yadyapi guṇasāmyātmani mūle krodheśvarāṣṭakaṃ tathāpi dhiyi tacchodhitamiti gaṇanāṃ na punaḥ prāptaṃ pratiṣṭhāyām

plain_english: Thus, in pratiṣṭhā, from the water tattva up to mūla, there are twenty-four tattvas, along with the satisfactions beginning with Ambā, those beginning with Tārā, and the siddhis beginning with Aṇimā.
sanskrit_cite: iti jalatattvānmūlaṃ tattvacaturviṃśatiḥ pratiṣṭhāyām ambādituṣṭivargastārādyāḥ siddhayo@ṇimādigaṇaḥ

plain_english: There are teachers, teachers with disciples, groups of seers, and those beginning with Iḍā, together with the eight bodies. There is also the world of modifications beginning with smell, the eight qualities of intellect, ego-activity, and the qualities of the sense objects.
sanskrit_cite: guravo guruśiṣyā ṛṣivarga iḍādiśca vigrahāṣṭakayuk gandhādivikārapuraṃ buddhiguṇāṣṭakamahaṃkriyā viṣayaguṇāḥ

plain_english: There is also the incidental group of twenty-seven beginning with Kāma, and likewise the groups of Gaṇeśas and Vidyeśas. Thus, among the bonds there are three worlds, and here in the puruṣa there are sixteen worlds.
sanskrit_cite: kāmādisaptaviṃśakamāgantu tathā gaṇeśavidyeśamayau iti pāśeṣu puratrayamitthaṃ puruṣe@tra bhuvanaṣoḍaśakam

plain_english: In the tattva of restriction there are ten Śaṅkara worlds; in time there are ten Śiva worlds, making two cities. In attachment there are the well-delighted world and the teacher-disciple city, and in the pair of knowledge and limited agency there are further worlds.
sanskrit_cite: niyatau śaṅkaradaśakaṃ kāle śivadaśakamiti puradvitayam rāge suhṛṣṭabhuvanaṃ guruśiṣyapuraṃ ca vitkalāyugale

plain_english: World after world is set out, including the three sheath-cities, the city of speech, and the city of measure. Thus vidyā, together with the seven tattvas beginning with puruṣa, contains twenty-seven cities.
sanskrit_cite: bhuvanaṃ bhuvanaṃ niśi puṭapuratrayaṃ vākpuraṃ pramāṇapuram iti saptaviṃśatipurā vidyā puruṣāditattvasaptakayuk

plain_english: In the pure domain are Vāmeśa, Rūpa, and Sūkṣma; then pure knowledge and the measure of Śakti’s radiance; then Suviśuddhi and Śiva, and the worlds named Mokṣa, Dhuva, Īśa, Saṃbuddha, Samaya, and Sauśiva.
sanskrit_cite: vāmeśarūpasūkṣmaṃ śuddhaṃ vidyātha śaktitejasvimitiḥ suviśuddhiśivau mokṣa dhuveṣisaṃbuddhasamayasauśivasaṃjñāḥ

plain_english: The peaceful level has seventeen cities. It includes the three cities of the Vidyeśas and Sadāśiva, the principles Bindu, Half-moon, and Nirodhikā, and reaches up to the supreme Sauśiva and the Indhikā and other cities of the central channel.
sanskrit_cite: saptadaśapurā śāntā vidyeśasadāśivapuratritayayuktā bindvardhendunirodhyaḥ parasauśivamindhikādipurasauṣumne

plain_english: There are the supreme sound, the cavity of Brahman, the upper Kuṇḍalinī joined with Sūkṣma and others, and Śakti; then come five cities supported by Vyāpin, Vyoman, Ananta, and Anātha.
sanskrit_cite: paranādo brahmabilaṃ sūkṣmādiyutordhvakuṇḍalī śaktiḥ vyāpivyomānantānāthānāśritapurāṇi pañca tataḥ

plain_english: Then there is a sixth, supported by Paramamanas. Alternatively, one may speak of the sixteen-world group of Samanā, or of the enclosure of Bindu, the supreme Sauśiva, and the five worlds beginning with Indhikā.
sanskrit_cite: ṣaṣṭhaṃ ca paramamanāśritamatha samanābhuvanaṣoḍaśī yadi vā bindvāvaraṇaṃ parasauśivaṃ ca pañcendhikādibhuvanāni

plain_english: The central-channel domain, the cavity of Brahman, Kuṇḍalinī, the five Vyāpins, and Samanā together make up this sixteen-world group. This is the pair of tattvas belonging to the level beyond peace.
sanskrit_cite: sauṣumnaṃ brahmabilaṃ kuṇḍalinī vyāpipañcakaṃ samanā iti ṣoḍaśabhuvaneyaṃ tattvayugaṃ śāntyatītā syāt

plain_english: In the revered Mataṅga scripture this sequence of cities is given: beginning with Kālāgni and the hells, it amounts principally to one hundred and forty.
sanskrit_cite: śrīmanmataṅgaśāstre ca kramo@yaṃ purapūgagaḥ kālāgnirnarakāḥ khābdhiyutaṃ mukhyatayā śatam

plain_english: Kūṣmāṇḍa, the seven netherworlds, the seven worlds, and Maheśvara make up the middle of the cosmic egg. Outside that, a hundred Rudras are situated.
sanskrit_cite: kūṣmāṇḍaḥ saptapātālī saptalokī maheśvaraḥ ityaṇḍamadhyaṃ tadbāhye śataṃ rudrā iti sthitāḥ

plain_english: There is a level of two hundred places joined with fifty-seven more. From the middle of a group of five eights, thirty-two are assigned within the four elements.
sanskrit_cite: sthānānāṃ dviśatī bhūmiḥ saptapañcāśatā yutā pañcāṣṭakasya madhyāddvātriṃśadbhūtacatuṣṭaye

plain_english: In the subtle elements there are five, and there are the Viśvedevas and then a group of eight. A fifth grouping is connected with the senses, egoity, intellect, and the guṇas, including a group of eight gods.
sanskrit_cite: tanmātreṣu ca pañca syurviśvedevāstato@ṣṭakam pañcamaṃ sendriye garve buddhau devāṣṭakaṃ guṇe

plain_english: In the root there is a group of eight yogas called Krodha, associated with time and with niyati. Patadruga and others, and Aṅguṣṭhamātra and others, belong to the tattva of attachment.
sanskrit_cite: yogāṣṭakaṃ krodhasaṃjñaṃ mūle kāle sanaiyate patadrugādyāścāṅguṣṭhamātrādyā rāgatattvagāḥ

plain_english: In vidyā there are twelve lords beginning with Ekaśiva, and in kalā there are ten. There is also a group of three hundred beginning with Vāmā, described by a numerical formula.
sanskrit_cite: dvādaśaikaśivādyāḥ syurvidyāyāṃ kalane daśa vāmādyāstriśatī seyaṃ triparvaṇyabdhirasyayuk

plain_english: Some Śaiva beings up to this point are summarized as belonging to Śrīkaṇṭha. When someone desires the enjoyments of others, the appropriate application should be made there.
sanskrit_cite: śaivāḥ kecidihānantāḥ śraikaṇṭhā iti saṃgrahaḥ yatra yadā parabhogān bubhukṣate tatra yojanaṃ kāryam

plain_english: When something is removed, purification should be done, and the rest should be treated as included within. This is shown as a scriptural variant set forth for that purpose.
sanskrit_cite: śodhanamatha taddhānau śeṣaṃ tvantargataṃ kāryam ityāgamaṃ prathayituṃ darśitametadvikalpitaṃ tena

plain_english: Teachers may also work out many other variants by their own understanding. In the revered former scripture, however, a count of one hundred and eighteen is stated.
sanskrit_cite: anye@pi bahuvikalpāḥ svadhiyācāryaiḥ samabhyūhyāḥ śrīpūrvaśāsane punaraṣṭādaśādhikaṃ śataṃ kathitam

plain_english: Here the text briefly states the chief matters to be purified. The list begins with Kālāgni, Kūṣmāṇḍa, Narakeśa, Hāṭaka, and Bhūtalapa.
sanskrit_cite: tadiha pradhānamadhikaṃ saṃkṣepeṇocyate śodhyam kālāgniḥ kūṣmāṇḍo narakeśo hāṭako@tha bhūtalapaḥ

plain_english: The list continues with Brahmā, the lord of the sage-world, and Rudras stationed in five intermediate regions. In the lower Ananta and in the east are those named Kapāli, Vahni, Anta, Nirṛti, and Bala.
sanskrit_cite: brahmā munilokeśo rudrāḥ pañcāntarālasthāḥ adhare@nantaḥ prācyāḥ kapālivahnyantanirṛtibalākhyāḥ

plain_english: The sequence runs upward through the named lords as far as Śambhu, together with the lord of Vīrabhadra. In the outer division of the Brahmāṇḍa there are eleven, and likewise five in the intermediate division.
sanskrit_cite: laghunidhipatividyādhipaśambhūrdhvāntaṃ savīrabhadrapati ekādaśabhirbāhye brahmāṇḍaṃ pañcabhistathāntarikaiḥ

plain_english: Thus this group of sixteen cities is to be considered in nivṛtti and kalā. The list begins with Lakulīśa, Bhārabhūti, Diṇḍi, Āṣāḍhi, Puṣkara, and Nimeṣa.
sanskrit_cite: iti ṣoḍaśapurametannivṛttikalayeha kalanīyam lakulīśabhārabhūtī diṇḍyāṣāḍhī ca puṣkaranimeṣau

plain_english: In the water principle, Prabhāsa and Sureśa are present for each self together with their retinues, along with Bhairava, Kedāra, Mahākāla, Madhyāmra, and Jalpa.
sanskrit_cite: prabhāsasureśāviti salile pratyātmakaṃ saparivāre bhairavakedāramahākālā madhyāmrajalpākhyāḥ

plain_english: In the principle of radiance is this secret group of eight: Śrīśaila, Hariścandra, and those named Bhīma, Indra, Aṭṭahāsa, Vimala, Kanakhala, Nakhala, Kuru, Sthita, and Gayā.
sanskrit_cite: śrīśailahariścandrāviti guhyāṣṭakamidaṃ mahasi bhīmendrāṭṭahāsavimalakanakhalanākhalakurusthitigayākhyāḥ

plain_english: This most secret group of eight is associated with wind, with the tanmātras, and with the witness. Its members include Sthāṇu, Suvarṇa, Bhadra, Gokarṇaka, and Mahālayaka.
sanskrit_cite: atiguhyāṣṭakametanmaruti ca satanmātrake ca sākṣe ca sthāṇusuvarṇākhyau kila bhadro gokarṇako mahālayakaḥ

plain_english: Avimukta, Rudrakoṭi, and Vastrāpada complete that pure group. In space are Sthūla, Sthūleśa, Śaṅku, Śruti, Kālañjara, and the bearer of the circle.
sanskrit_cite: avimuktarudrakoṭī vastrāpada ityadaḥ pavitraṃ khe sthūlasthūleśaśaṅkuśrutikālañjarāśca maṇḍalabhṛt

plain_english: In the ego-principle there is a group of eight including Mākoṭa, the two Aṇḍas, and Chagalāṇḍa. Others also say that the tanmātras and the senses extend up to ahaṅkāra.
sanskrit_cite: mākoṭāṇḍadvitayacchagalāṇḍā aṣṭakaṃ hyahaṅkāre anye@haṅkārāntastanmātrāṇīndriyāṇi cāpyāhuḥ

plain_english: In intellect the group of eight sources is taught, and in primal nature the group of eight yogas beginning with Akṛta. Thus the established order consists of seven groups of eight worlds, extending from water up to the root.
sanskrit_cite: dhiyi yonyaṣṭakamuktaṃ prakṛtau yogāṣṭakaṃ kilākṛtaprabhṛti iti saptāṣṭakabhuvanā pratiṣṭhitiḥ salilato hi mūlāntā

plain_english: In the human principle are Vāma, Bhīma, Ugra, Bhaveśa, Vīra, Pracaṇḍa, Gaurīśa, Aja, Ananta, and Ekaśiva. In vidyā there is the pair Krodha and Caṇḍa.
sanskrit_cite: nari vāmo bhīmograu bhaveśavīrāḥ pracaṇḍagaurīśau ajasānantaikaśivau vidyāyāṃ krodhacaṇḍayugmaṃ syāt

plain_english: In kalā and niyati are Saṃvarta and Jyotiratha, and also Sūra and Pañcānta. In kāla is the triad named Vīra, Śikhīśa, and Śrīkaṇṭha.
sanskrit_cite: saṃvarto jyotiratho kalāniyatyāṃ ca sūrapañcāntau vīraśikhīśaśrīkaṇṭhasaṃjñametattrayaṃ ca kāle syāt

plain_english: These eight, led by Bhuvaneśa, are situated in the night division and in the thumb: Vāma with Mahātejā, Bhavodbhava, Ekapinga, Īśāna, and the rest of that group.
sanskrit_cite: samahātejā vāmo bhavodbhavaścaikapiṅgaleśānau bhuvaneśapuraḥsarakāvaṅguṣṭha ime niśi sthitā hyaṣṭau

plain_english: Vidyā has twenty-eight worlds, extending from puruṣa to the end of night. There are Hālāhala, Rudra, Krud, Ambikā, Aghorikā, and Vāmā.
sanskrit_cite: aṣṭāviṃśatibhuvanā vidyā puruṣānniśāntamiyam hālāhalarudrakrudambikāghorikāḥ savāmāḥ syuḥ

plain_english: In vidyā are the Vidyeśvaras, and in Īśa there are eight. In Sadāśiva there are five: Vāmā, Jyeṣṭhā, Raudrī, Śakti, and Sakalā. This is the peaceful level.
sanskrit_cite: vidyāyāṃ vidyeśāstvaṣṭāvīśe sadāśive pañca vāmā jyeṣṭhā raudrī śaktiḥ sakalā ca śontayam

plain_english: Śāntyatītā consists of eighteen worlds, yet it is also itself a world. Thus the division of the path of space has been told, as instructed by revered Śambhu.
sanskrit_cite: aṣṭādaśa bhuvanā syāt śāntyatītā tvabhuvanaiva iti deśādhvavibhāgaḥ kathitaḥ śrīśambhunā samādiṣṭaḥ
